A total of PS174 million was paid out, up from PS130 million the previous season. Manchester City were the biggest spenders, paying out PS26.3 million, followed by Chelsea (PS25.1 million) and Liverpool (PS23.2 million). The figures come from the Premier League's annual report on agent fees, which shows that clubs spent more than PS500 million on agents over the past five years. The report also revealed that almost half (48.9) of the money went to agents based in England and Wales, while 16.4 went to agents based abroad. The highest individual payment made to an agent was PS8.1 million, paid by Chelsea to Pini Zahavi. The report comes amid growing scrutiny of agent fees, with some football clubs and supporters calling for greater transparency and regulation of the industry.

She had come prepared to own up to her mistakes, apologising to the gathered throng just as a few hours earlier she had apologised to the cabinet. It had been a mistake, she told them. A mistake to lead the country into the European Union on false pretences, a mistake to try to hide the truth from the people. "I know I have made mistakes and I am sorry they have hurt you," she said. "The pain is all mine. For this I deeply and profoundly regret." But just as she was making a decent stab of it, her husband, Denis, turned up and took over the show. It was Denis, who had been her rock during the whole affair, who would now be there for her in retirement, he said. And then he went off into a digression about his work that lasted several minutes. Everyone seemed to be enjoying themselves immensely. Mrs Thatcher was looking pained but amused. Her daughter, Carol, was clutching a handkerchief and grinning broadly. But the question remained: what next? If the end of Mrs Thatcher's reign for the moment seems to signal the triumph of Europe over the eurosceptics, this does not necessarily mean that Britain will rush back into the heart of the EU. On the contrary, the incoming prime minister John Major is unlikely to be any more enthusiastic about European integration than his predecessor. Mr Major is also likely to find himself under pressure from a new breed of Eurosceptic Conservative MPs, many of whom were elected at the last election. There are now 50 or so strongly anti-EU Conservative MPs and another 20 or so mildly Eurosceptic ones. Mr Major may feel obliged to listen to them if only to stop them causing trouble. Most of those who have been chosen as vice-chairmen of the Conservative Party will be from this group, according to one Eurosceptic MP. Even some cabinet ministers are thought to be less than enthusiastic about the project - such as Michael Portillo, who, although he supported Mrs Thatcher's leadership bid, is thought to be sceptical about the single market, and Peter Lilley, who was a member of the committee that recommended against joining the European Exchange Rate Mechanism. So perhaps Mrs Thatcher's resignation will eventually come to be seen as the beginning of the end of the British obsession with Europe. Or at least, the beginning of the end of the British passion for forging ahead with European integration at all costs.

In 1881, Tesla moved to Budapest to work under Ferenc Puskas at a telegraph company, the Budapest Telephone Exchange. Upon arrival, Tesla realized that the company, then under construction, was inefficient. He contributed to the design of an improved arc lamp and transformer, which was patented in 1883. The next year he patented an induction motor, which ran on alternating current (AC). In 1886, Tesla visited Edison in New York, hoping to interest him in his AC system. Edison, who favored direct current (DC), did not see any value in Tesla's ideas. Disheartened, Tesla took a job digging ditches for 2 per day. At this low point, Tesla met Alfred S. Brown, one of the founders of the Western Union Telegraph Company. Brown was impressed by Tesla's ideas and put him in charge of building a power station on Long Island to supply electricity to New York City. The station opened in January 1887. Tesla continued to refine his ideas for an AC system. In 1888, he formed the Tesla Electric Company to develop them. The same year, he demonstrated the first AC induction motor. In 1891, Tesla established the Tesla Electric Light Company to market his inventions. That year, he also designed a high-frequency AC dynamo, or generator. Tesla's alternating current system was superior to Edison's DC system in several ways. For one thing, it could carry electricity long distances with little loss of power. AC also could be used safely for household appliances, because it did not produce sparks that could cause fires. However, some people were afraid of being electrocuted by AC. To allay these fears, Tesla staged a public demonstration in 1893 in which he passed electrical current through his own body. In 1895, Tesla opened the first hydroelectric power plant in the United States at Niagara Falls. This plant provided electricity to Buffalo, New York, and other cities in the region. In 1897, the Tesla Electric Company merged with another firm to become the General Electric Company. With the merger, Tesla lost control of his AC system. He parted company with General Electric in 1899. Tesla continued to work on new electrical inventions. He also devoted time to trying to harness the power of Niagara Falls to provide electricity to New York City. These projects consumed so much of his time and money that he often had difficulty meeting his expenses. By the early 1900s, Tesla was more famous for his unusual ideas than for his practical inventions. These included plans for a "death ray" that could project energy through the air to destroy enemy targets, a "world system" for transmitting electricity and messages without wires, and "teleforce," a device that could move objects from a distance. Tesla also wrote about flying machines and robots. Tesla died in New York City on January 7, 1943.

The tech giant has said that it has received 26 reports of the affected batteries overheating, including five reports of minor burns and one case of smoke inhalation. The recall has been of great concern to Apple as it has openly prioritized the safety of the customers over making huge sums of money from the sale of their products. The safety of its customers remains their top priority. Affected customers are urged to stop using the laptops immediately and to contact Apple to have their battery replaced for free. Apple has created a dedicated webpage for the recall process where customers can enter their MacBook Pro serial number to determine if their computer needs a new battery. Apple has apologized for any inconvenience the recall may cause and is encouraging affected customers to contact them as soon as possible. Any customer whose 15in MacBook Pro has been affected is urged to contact Apple either on the phone, via email, or by visiting an Apple store to get the battery replaced free of charge.

Factory activity in China shrank significantly more than expected in July, according to recent data released by the country's National Bureau of Statistics. This marks the weakest performance since July 2016 and signals a further economic slowdown in the world's second largest economy. The Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), a measure of factory activity, fell to 49.7 in July from 50.0 the month before. A reading below 50 indicates contraction in the sector. The decline was largely attributed to a decrease in new orders, which fell to 48.2 from 50.2 in June. According to analysts, this suggests that Chinese exporters are struggling to maintain their sales amid the escalating trade war with the United States. The news comes as a disappointment for Chinese policymakers who had been hoping for some signs of improvement in the manufacturing sector. In recent months, officials have implemented measures such as tax cuts and looser monetary policy to help stimulate economic growth. However, these efforts appear to have had limited impact on the manufacturing sector so far. The slowdown in China's manufacturing sector is likely to have broader implications for global growth. China is the world's largest exporter and its weak performance could lead to a drag on global demand. This could pose a challenge to other economies that rely heavily on Chinese exports. Analysts say that China will need to take further steps if it wants to reverse the current trend. These could include relaxing credit restrictions and ramping up government spending on infrastructure projects. It remains to be seen how effective these policies will be in helping to revive the Chinese economy.

By investing in treatments and cures for these illnesses, we can help to prevent future healthcare costs and even save lives. Finally, as a society, we have a moral obligation to care for those who are most vulnerable and in need, including children with chronic illnesses. Thus, we should invest in public resources to ensure that all children have access to the care they need to thrive and live healthy, fulfilling lives.

The seahorse placenta is a fascinating example of convergent evolution. Male seahorses' brood pouches develop and function like human placentas. The seahorse's placenta is very different from ours in terms of structure and function. For example, the seahorse placenta is not as efficient at exchanging oxygen and nutrients between the mother and the embryo. However, it is still an amazing example of how different species can evolve similar structures to solve similar problems.

Behavioural economists have shown that people are often averse to inequality and will make choices to avoid unequal outcomes. In this paper, we consider how to allocate indivisible goods fairly That's an interesting topic. In the context of indivisible goods, fairness can be a complex issue. One approach that has been suggested is the "random assignment" approach, where parties agree to a fair distribution by randomly assigning the goods. Another approach is the "auction" approach, where the goods are allocated to the bidder who is willing to pay the highest price. However, both these approaches have limitations and may not always result in a fair distribution. Another approach that has gained popularity in recent years is the "priority-based" approach, where individuals are assigned priority based on some criteria such as need or merit. This approach ensures that the individuals who are most deserving or in need of the goods are allocated them first. Ultimately, the choice of allocation method depends on the specific circumstances and the values of the parties involved.

There's a part of your brain, lets call him bob. Bob is a very particular fellow, in fact so particular that when he see something he doesn't like he lets you know. He might tell you that a person is mean, when in reality they're actually quite friendly. The problem is, that even when bob is wrong, you still can't help but listen to him. In October 1529, Philip I, Landgrave of Hesse, convoked an assembly of German and Swiss theologians at the Marburg Colloquy, to establish doctrinal unity in the emerging Protestant states. Agreement was reached on 14 of the 15 articles discussed, but a disagreement on the nature of the Eucharist (communion) could not be resolved between Martin Luther, the leader of the German Reformation, and Ulrich Zwingli, the leader of the Swiss Reformation. This led to a split between Lutherans (who believed in the real presence of Christ in the Eucharist) and the Reformed (who believed in a symbolic interpretation of the Eucharist). However, the Marburg Colloquy still paved the way for greater unity among the Protestant churches in Germany and Switzerland.

The paper deals with the problem of deciding if two finite-dimensional linear subspaces over an arbitrary field are identical up to a permutation of the coordinates. This problem is referred to as the subspace isomorphism problem. The paper presents a novel algorithm for solving this problem efficiently. The algorithm uses a combination of linear algebra techniques and graph theory to compute a canonical form for the subspaces, which can then be compared for equivalence. The paper begins by introducing the subspace isomorphism problem and discussing its relevance in various applications. It then describes the algorithm in detail, explaining each step and providing theoretical analysis of its complexity. The authors also present experimental results showing the effectiveness of the algorithm in practice. The main contribution of the paper is a new and efficient approach to solving the subspace isomorphism problem. The algorithm is based on a unique combination of linear algebra and graph theory, and is able to compute a canonical form for subspaces that can be compared for isomorphism. Many people have a poor estimation of where the front of their car is. In left-turn lanes, it's a good idea to stop well short of the line in case the drivers in front of you don't realize they're supposed to stop there. You may think that you have room to pull through, but remember: don't be a jerk and block the intersection. Allow Extra Time This is probably the most important tip when driving in winter weather. Slippery roads mean driver reactions times are longer, so you need to anticipate things ahead of you. Allow yourself extra time to get where you're going. This will help you stay calm and relaxed while driving, which keeps stress levels down and makes it easier to react to sudden changes. When in doubt, go slow. Drive Defensively In addition to giving yourself extra time to get places, always drive defensively. Watch for red lights, brake early, turn slowly, and look for potential problems on the road. If you're about to hit black ice, for example, it's better to swerve out of the way than to try and brake. Just remember: don't swerve into someone else! Leave More Distance Again, because slippery roads mean longer reaction times and less control over your car, you should leave more space between your car and the one ahead of you. If they have to stop suddenly, you don't want to hit them. It's best to keep at least four seconds of space between you and the car in front of you. But if visibility is low (say, if it's raining or snowing), then you'll want to leave even more space. Know When To Use Your Brakes When the roads are icy, you need to learn how to use your brakes correctly. The best way to do this is to practice braking on your driveway or another safe spot first. Once you've figured out what method works best, use it whenever you're on an icy road. Get to know your brakes, and know what kind of pressure you need to apply to them to stop effectively. If you're still unsure of how to handle icy roads, you can always call us. We'd love to help you.

Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged recently as a promising application of deep neural networks to the numerical solution of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs). However, the original PINN algorithm suffers from a lack of interpretability and an inability to generalize to new or unseen domains. To address these limitations, several extensions to the original PINN algorithm have been proposed. For example, physics-constrained neural networks (PCNNs) enforce physical constraints at every point in the domain, while adversarial PINNs use adversarial training to improve generalization. Other approaches include incorporating regularization or enforcing constraints on the network weights or activations to ensure physical consistency. Overall, PINNs are a promising tool for solving complex physical problems, but careful consideration must be given to the specific problem at hand and the best approach for incorporating physical constraints into the neural network architecture.

In less than a minute, everything had returned to normal; my little cottage being buried under a mound of green gooey mush. I'm sure that you're wondering why I didn't try to run away when I heard the screaming. The answer is simple: I was frozen with fear. I couldn't move, I couldn't speak, I couldn't even think. All I could do was sit there and watch as the jell-o advanced on my home. When it was all over, I was covered in green slime from head to toe. It took me hours to clean myself off, and even longer to clean the cottage. As for the jell-o, it's still out there somewhere. Sophie couldn't believe it as she stood in front of the mirror, staring at her reflection. Today was the day she had been waiting for ever since she first heard about it - her 18th birthday. This was the day when she would finally receive her superpower. Like every other teenager in her world, Sophie had spent hours imagining what her power might be. Maybe she would be able to fly, or turn invisible, or shoot fireballs from her fingertips. The possibilities were endless, and she couldn't wait to find out what her power would be. But as the clock ticked down to midnight, Sophie's excitement turned to fear. What if her power wasn't cool, or useful, or even safe? What if she was stuck with something she didn't want, something that would make her an outcast among her peers? At the stroke of midnight, Sophie felt a strange sensation in her body, like the fluttering of hundreds of butterflies in her stomach. She closed her eyes and waited for the transformation to be complete. When she opened her eyes again, she saw that she was still staring at her own reflection. But something was different. Something was very, very wrong. Sophie screamed in horror as she saw what her power was. She had been given the ability to make people feel intense physical pain just by looking at them. It was a power that no one would want to have, a power that would make her a monster in the eyes of everyone around her. Sophie tried to control her power, to hold it back and not let it affect anyone else. But the more she tried to suppress it, the more it grew within her, burning her from the inside out. As the days went by, Sophie became more and more isolated. She could no longer look at anyone without causing them pain, and so she had to spend all her time alone. She wished with all her heart that she had never been given this power, that she could go back to being an ordinary girl. But there was no going back. Sophie was stuck with her power, for better or for worse. And so she had to learn to live with it, to make the best of what she had been given. It wasn't easy, and it wasn't pleasant, but Sophie knew that she had to try. She had a power that no one else had, and she had to find a way to use it for good. Maybe someday she would even learn to embrace her power, to see it as a blessing rather than a curse. But for now, all Sophie could do was keep her head down and soldier on, hoping that someday the world would see her as something other than a freak.

The train also features regenerative braking technology, which captures energy produced by the brakes and turns it into additional power for the train. According to the train's creators, this innovative charging system makes the Infinity Train the world's first train to create its own electricity from gravity. The train doesn't require overhead power lines or other external power sources, making it more efficient and sustainable. The train was developed by a team of engineers and scientists working in partnership to create a new, more sustainable transportation option. The group hopes that the Infinity Train will pave the way for more sustainable public transportation options in the future. "Our goal in developing the Infinity Train was to create a truly sustainable train that has a positive impact on the environment and provides a reliable, efficient transportation option for commuters," said the lead engineer on the project. "We believe that this new charging technology has the potential to change the way we think about transportation and energy use." The Infinity Train is slated to begin testing later this year, with hopes of rolling out to the public in the near future. The train is expected to be a major milestone in the fight against climate change and a sign of the growing innovation and creativity that is driving sustainable energy development.

Wireless communications are vulnerable against radio frequency (RF) jamming which might be caused either intentionally or unintentionally. A particular subset of wireless networks, vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANET) which incorporate a large number of vehicles equipped with wireless communication devices, are particularly susceptible to RF jamming attacks. Such attacks can disrupt critical safety applications in VANETs that rely on timely and accurate information exchange between vehicles, such as collision avoidance and road safety warnings. To mitigate the impact of RF jamming attacks, various countermeasures can be employed. One approach is to use frequency hopping techniques, where the wireless devices switch between different channels at regular intervals, making it harder for an attacker to jam all channels simultaneously. Another approach is to use directional antennas that can focus the signal in a specific direction, making it harder for an attacker to disrupt the communication between two neighboring vehicles. Additionally, the use of cryptographic techniques can also provide protection to wireless transmissions and prevent attackers from intercepting or modifying the messages. Overall, it is important to implement a combination of these countermeasures to ensure the security and reliability of wireless communications in VANETs.

Oil prices dropped to their lowest level in 11 years on Monday, as global production remains consistently high. Crude oil futures for January delivery fell to 33.84 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), its lowest price since February 2009. It was the fifth consecutive day of losses for the commodity and its biggest one-day drop since late August. The continued slump in oil prices is due to a variety of factors, including a relentless rise in global production and little sign of demand picking up. The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), which accounts for 40 percent of global oil supply, has increased output to record levels of around 33 million barrels a day. The group, led by Saudi Arabia, has refused to cut production in the face of falling prices, instead choosing to defend its market share. This has caused a glut in global supply, pushing prices down further. Meanwhile, weak economic growth in emerging markets such as China, India, and Brazil has weighed on demand for crude. As these economies struggle, they have reduced their imports of oil, further contributing to the oversupply. Analysts expect oil prices to remain low for some time, with some predicting that it could dip even lower. U.S. bank JP Morgan estimates that prices could fall to 20 a barrel if OPEC continues to produce at current levels. The prolonged slump in oil prices has had a damaging effect on many countries' economies. In Russia for example, the ruble has lost about half its value against the dollar due to falling oil revenues. The impact of the price drop has also been felt by many businesses. Oil producers in North America, where extraction costs are relatively high compared to other countries, have been hit particularly hard. Despite the continued drop in prices, some analysts believe there are signs of hope. A report from Goldman Sachs suggests that the global oil supply and demand balance may start to improve over the next few months. It remains to be seen whether this will be enough to stop prices from dropping further. In the meantime, global production levels look set to remain at unprecedented highs, putting more pressure on an already fragile market.

The job search process can be daunting for many people, especially those considering a career in tech. With the ever-changing landscape of technology and the competition for tech jobs at an all-time high, it's important to be prepared for your job search and make sure you stand out from the crowd. Here are some lessons learned from a tech job search that will help you succeed. 1. Know Your Skills and Strengths: Before you start your job search, take the time to understand what skills and strengths you possess that would benefit a prospective employer. This could include programming languages, database systems, web development, and other related technical topics. Knowing what you bring to the table will give you a better chance of landing a job. 2. Research Companies and Industries: Take the time to research companies and industries related to the field you are interested in pursuing. Doing so will enable you to tailor your resume and cover letter to showcase the skills you have that would be beneficial to the company. It's also a good idea to stay up to date on industry news and trends, as this will provide you with valuable information when interviewing. 3. Network: Networking is key in any job search. Don't be afraid to reach out to people in your industry and ask them questions. You never know who might have connections that could help you land a job. Additionally, attending meetups and conferences is another great way to network and build relationships. 4. Utilize Job Sites and Social Media: Technology has made it easier than ever to search for jobs, so take advantage of these resources. Use job sites such as Indeed, Monster, and Glassdoor to find potential openings. Additionally, don't forget about social media. Platforms such as LinkedIn, Twitter, and Facebook are excellent ways to connect with potential employers and make yourself known. 5. Prepare for Interviews: Once you've landed an interview, it's important to be prepared. Research the company, practice answering commonly asked questions, and come up with questions to ask the interviewer. It's also helpful to have examples of projects you've worked on or challenges you've faced to illustrate your experience and capabilities. By following these tips, you'll be better equipped to tackle the tech job search. With the right mindset and preparation, you can increase your chances of success. Good luck!

In this paper, we present a novel approach to machine reading comprehension for the MS-MARCO dataset. Unlike the SQuAD dataset that aims to answer a question with exact text spans from a given context, the MS-MARCO dataset requires systems to generate a full answer from scratch. We propose a two-stage machine reading comprehension system based on a pointer-generator network and a language model with pre-trained BERT parameters. In the first stage, we use the pointer-generator network to extract important keywords from the query and the context paragraphs. The keywords are then used as input for the second stage, which is a language model fine-tuned using BERT parameters. The output of this language model is a full answer generated from the extracted keywords. Our experiments show that our approach achieves an F1 score of 0.41 on the MS-MARCO development set. This result is comparable to state-of-the-art approaches, demonstrating the effectiveness of our proposed method.

Storage systems have a strong need for substantially improving their error correction capabilities, especially for long-term storage where the accumulating errors can exceed the decoding threshold of error-correcting codes (ECCs). To address this need, researchers have developed advanced ECC techniques such as low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes and their variations. These techniques are highly efficient in terms of the number of bits used to represent data and the amount of overhead required for error correction. In addition, new technologies such as flash memory and 3D NAND have emerged that provide higher storage densities and faster access times. These new technologies require sophisticated error correction capabilities, which are addressed by even more advanced ECC techniques such as turbo codes and space-time codes. Finally, new storage architectures such as RAID have been introduced to provide better reliability and increased scalability. To ensure data integrity, these architectures rely on sophisticated ECC techniques such as Reed-Solomon codes.

In recent years, a new genre of art has been emerging from the depths of the creative psyche. Alien Dreams, as it's being called, is a style of art that draws inspiration from the possibility of extraterrestrial life and the mythical creatures and worlds of science fiction. Artists who are pioneering this new style say that it represents a departure from traditional art forms, and allows them to explore the outer limits of their imagination. They see the concept of alien life as a blank canvas, upon which they can paint their dreams and visions of what otherworldly creatures might look like. One artist, Mina Zingara, says that Alien Dreams has given her the freedom to express herself in ways she never thought possible. "I always felt like I was an outsider in the traditional art world," she says. "But with Alien Dreams, I can let my imagination run wild and create something truly unique." Zingara's work is a perfect example of the style. Her pieces often feature humanoid creatures with glowing eyes, trailing tendrils and bizarre appendages, set against a backdrop of far-off planets and boiling nebulas. They have a surreal, dreamlike quality that evokes the work of Salvador Dali or Rene Magritte. Another artist, Delta Vega, sees Alien Dreams as a way to explore philosophical questions about the nature of existence. "If there are other intelligent beings out there in the universe, what does that say about us?" he asks. "It's a question that has fascinated us for centuries, and I think we're getting closer and closer to finding the answer." Vega's work often combines elements of traditional sci-fi with abstract art, creating a surreal, otherworldly vista that seems to border on the edge of madness. The analysis techniques of system log messages (syslog messages) have a long history from when the syslog mechanism was invented. Typically, the analysis consists of two parts, one is a static analysis and the other is a dynamic analysis. The static analysis consists of analyzing system log messages, without any context-based information, to detect known attack patterns. There are several approaches to performing this type of analysis, including simple statistical methods and more sophisticated data mining techniques. The dynamic analysis consists of analyzing system log messages together with other context information (e.g., user behavior) to detect attacks. In this paper, we focus on the static analysis of system log messages for security purposes. There are several challenges in analyzing system log messages for security purposes. One is that system log messages are typically unstructured text, which makes it difficult to extract useful information from them. Another challenge is that system log messages can be generated by different devices and software applications, which can lead to a large number of different message formats. This can make it difficult to develop a single analysis approach that can be used for all messages. Finally, system log messages can be generated by both legitimate and malicious activity, which can make it difficult to distinguish between the two. In this paper, we survey existing approaches for analyzing system log messages for security purposes. We categorize these approaches into five main categories: rule-based approaches, statistical approaches, data mining approaches, hybrid approaches, and visualization approaches. For each category, we discuss the main methods that have been proposed and evaluate their strengths and weaknesses. We also discuss some of the challenges that remain in this area.

Search is a central problem in artificial intelligence, and BFS and DFS the two most fundamental ways to search. In this report we derive results for average BFS and DFS search times on random graphs. We consider undirected graphs with n vertices and m edges, where each edge is chosen independently with probability p. We assume that the graph is connected, meaning that every vertex is reachable from every other vertex. We first consider BFS. Starting at a given vertex s, BFS visits all vertices in increasing order of distance from s. The algorithm maintains a queue of vertices to visit next, initially containing only s. At each step, it removes the first vertex from the queue, adds all its neighbors that have not yet been visited to the end of the queue, and marks it as visited. We model BFS as follows. For each vertex v, we associate a random variable Xv that is the distance from s to v in the graph. We assume that Xs 0 and that Xv is infinite if v is not reachable from s. Our goal is to compute the expected value E[Xv] for each v. To compute E[Xv], we use the "one step" property of BFS. I have been noticing the news about police officers shooting children or innocent people mistakely, and causing death or serious injuries a lot. So I thought, why would a police officer do that? It's important to acknowledge that not all police officers act in this way and that the vast majority of police officers do their jobs with integrity and professionalism. However, when incidents like these do occur, there can be a variety of factors at play. One possible factor is a lack of adequate training or resources. Police officers are often the first responders in high-pressure situations that can escalate quickly, and they need to be equipped to make split-second decisions in highly stressful and dangerous situations. If they don't have the appropriate training or resources, they may be more likely to make mistakes or use excessive force. Another factor is the culture within law enforcement agencies. There have been cases where officers who have used excessive force or acted inappropriately have not faced consequences for their actions. This can create a culture of impunity, where officers feel that they can act with impunity and without fear of consequences. Additionally, implicit biases may come into play. Many police officers are trained to be vigilant and look out for signs of danger, and this can often be useful. However, if they have implicit biases against certain groups of people, they may be more likely to see them as threatening or dangerous, even if there is no evidence to support that perception. Overall, it's necessary to invest in better training and resources for police officers, to create a culture of accountability and consequences for wrongdoing, and to continue working to address implicit biases within law enforcement.

Scientists have made an incredible discovery in Antarctica - an egg that belonged to an ancient sea monster. This is the first time such a creature has been found in the frozen continent, and it is expected to help shed light on the history of the region. The egg, which is estimated to be around 68 million years old, was found by a group of researchers digging in the James Ross Island area of Antarctica. The area is known for its rich deposits of fossils, but this is the first time anything of this type has been found in the region. After careful analysis, the scientists have identified the egg as belonging to a mosasaur, a type of marine reptile that was once common in the seas that covered the planet during the time of the dinosaurs. These creatures could grow up to 50 feet long and were known for their sharp teeth and powerful jaws. The discovery has been hailed as a major breakthrough in understanding the history of Antarctica. Previously, it was thought that the area was covered in ice during the time of the dinosaurs and that few creatures could have survived in such harsh conditions. However, this discovery suggests that the region was actually much more hospitable than previously believed. The team of researchers is now planning to conduct further studies on the egg to learn more about the creature that laid it. They are hoping that this discovery could lead to more insights into the ecological history of Antarctica and help us to better understand the evolution of life on our planet.

The authors begin by introducing the necessary mathematical background, including the definition of linear subspaces as well as their bases and dimensions. They then discuss the basic idea behind their proposed solution, which relies on the fact that two subspaces over an arbitrary field are identical up to a permutation of the coordinates if and only if their bases are related by a permutation matrix. Using this concept, the authors propose an algorithm for solving the subspace identification problem. The algorithm first computes the dimension of each subspace and checks if they are equal. If they are not, then the subspaces cannot be identical. If they are equal, then the algorithm uses a series of matrix operations to determine if the bases of the subspaces are permutations of each other. Finally, the authors provide an example to illustrate how the proposed algorithm works. They also discuss possible extensions of the algorithm and its efficiency in comparison with existing algorithms. Overall, the paper presents a useful solution to the subspace identification problem using algebraic techniques. The authors provide a clear explanation of the proposed algorithm and demonstrate its efficacy through an example. Furthermore, their discussion of possible extensions of the algorithm and its efficiency in comparison with existing algorithms makes the paper a valuable resource for researchers interested in this topic.

Research suggests women will not earn as much as their male counterparts until 2069, nearly 100 years after the Equal Pay Act was introduced in 1970. Holyrood's economy, fair work and jobs committee has written to the Scottish government asking for information on what action it is taking to close the gap. It also wants to know about the impact of Brexit on women's employment. Labour MSP Alex Rowley, who sits on the committee, said: "We live in a society where gender stereotypes are still prevalent and jobs with a female-stereotype are paid less than male-stereotyped jobs. Women are still more likely to work part-time and they are likely to be worse affected by zero-hours contracts as they tend to use them to fit in with other caring responsibilities. "It is therefore right that this Parliament takes steps to ensure that our laws are fit for purpose in relation to equal pay to ensure we close the pay gap once and for all." Convener Gordon Lindhurst added: "We need to see a greater focus on this issue and I look forward to receiving evidence from the Scottish government and the Equality and Human Rights Commission later this month." A Scottish government spokeswoman said: "We are committed to achieving gender equality and have implemented a number of policies to support this. "Our Gender Pay Gap Action Plan focuses on the actions that employers can take to help eliminate the gender pay gap and we have established an independent expert group to consider the most effective way to deliver equal pay for work of equal value."

Solana is a proof-of-stake blockchain with a mechanism called proof-of-history. This article is a guide on how to build a full stack dapp using Solana. Write smart contracts: Smart contracts are code that runs on the blockchain and defines the rules of your application. You can write smart contracts for Solana using the Rust programming language and the Solana SDK. 4. Build the backend: The backend of your application will interact with the smart contracts and store data on the blockchain. You can use Node.js and Solana SDK to develop the backend. 5. Construct the frontend: The frontend of your application will provide a user interface for users to interact with your dapp. You can use React and Solana Web3.js to create the frontend. 6. Deploy your dapp: Once your dapp is complete, you can deploy it to the Solana blockchain. You will need to pay a small fee for the transaction to be processed on the blockchain. 7. Test and iterate: It's essential to test your application thoroughly before launching it to users. You can use testing frameworks such as Mocha and Chai to test your smart contracts and frontend. In conclusion, building a dapp on Solana requires knowledge of web development technologies, Solidity, and Rust. In this position paper we present a novel approach to neurobiologically plausible implementation of emotional reactions and behaviors for real-time autonomous robotic systems. The working metaphor we use is the notion of the "emotional brain," which is based on the idea that emotions are a result of different brain regions interacting in a dynamic manner. We present a hierarchical model where the emotional brain can be broken down into three distinct layers: an emotion layer, a control layer, and a behavior layer. At the emotion layer, we propose using neurobiologically plausible models to simulate emotional states such as fear, anger, joy, or surprise. These emotional states would be represented by a set of parameters that characterize the degree of each state. The control layer would then use these emotional states to regulate behavior. For example, when presented with a fearful situation, the robot's behavior would be regulated so as to avoid it, whereas if presented with a joyful situation, the robot's behavior would be likely to move towards it. Finally, at the behavior layer, the robot would act upon the decisions made at the control layer by executing specific motor commands. The proposed system has several advantages over traditional approaches to robotic emotion. First, it provides a biologically plausible mechanism for generating realistic emotional reactions. Second, it offers flexibility in terms of behaviors generated, since any desired behavior can be specified in terms of the parameters at the emotion layer. Finally, the modularity of the system allows for easy optimization of individual components, making it possible to create robots that display subtle and complex emotional responses. We believe that our proposed approach could provide a powerful tool for creating autonomous robots that exhibit realistic emotional responses and behaviors. We hope that our ideas will stimulate further research into this area and aid in the development of more sophisticated robotic systems.

Conduct an experimental study- In an experimental study, the researcher manipulates the independent variable, observes the dependent variable, and controls extraneous variables. Experimental studies can establish causation. 2. Use a control group- Control groups help determine if the results are due to the independent variable or other extraneous factors. 3. The 2007 Lisbon Treaty explicitly recognised fundamental rights by providing in Article 6 (1) that "The Union recognises the rights, freedoms and principles set out in the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union of 7 December 2000, as adapted at Strasbourg, on 12 December 2007, which shall have the same legal value as the Treaties." The Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union (CFR) is the EU's most comprehensive document on human rights. It was created in 2000 and entered into force after the Treaty of Lisbon was ratified in 2009. The CFR outlines a range of civil, political, economic and social rights for all people in the EU. Its contents draw from the European Convention on Human Rights, the UN Declaration of Human Rights, and other international conventions. It also includes rights such as data protection, gender equality, the right to good administration, and the right to free movement. By recognising these rights, the EU has taken a major step in safeguarding the fundamental freedoms of its citizens.

He realized that perfection was not the ultimate goal, but being true to oneself was.

While it is true that not all examples of cultural appropriation are intended to be derogatory or offensive, it is essential to recognize that such appropriation often contributes to the wider system of cultural erasure and marginalization. Rather than honoring or respecting the cultures being borrowed from, cultural appropriation often reduces them to mere costume or trend, ignoring their complex histories and meanings. This can not only perpetuate harmful stereotypes but also undermines the ownership and control that members of those cultures should have over their own identities and representation. Moreover, dismissing the concerns and experiences of those who are offended by cultural appropriation only serves to perpetuate a cycle of cultural dominance and privilege, which ultimately harms us all. Instead of ignoring or minimizing the impact of cultural appropriation, we should strive to learn more about the cultures and individuals it affects, and work to create more inclusive and respectful ways of engaging with and celebrating diversity.

According to the study, these people are believed to have split off from other human populations around 36,000 years ago and migrated into Europe, where they interbred with early European hunter-gatherers. The research showed that the "Basal Eurasians" were one of the founding populations of Europe, along with early farmers and hunter-gatherers. Scientists had previously identified the genetic contributions of these two groups, but the role of the "Basal Eurasians" was unknown until now. "Our data suggest that Basal Eurasians represent a previously unrecognized source of ancestry in Europe," says the lead author of the study, Professor David Reich of Harvard Medical School. "They are a long-lost branch of the human family tree, and their contribution to the modern European gene pool is remarkable." The discovery of this fourth ancestral "tribe" is significant because it sheds new light on the ancient history of Europe and the movements of its people. It also provides a more complete picture of the genetic diversity of modern Europeans, which has been shaped by millennia of migration and interbreeding. The researchers say that the genetic legacy of the "Basal Eurasians" can still be seen in some modern European populations, particularly in the Iberian Peninsula and the Caucasus. The study also highlights the power of genomic DNA analysis to uncover previously unknown information about our past. As the technology continues to improve, scientists expect to make even more discoveries about the history of humanity and our complex genetic inheritance.

Crowd counting from unconstrained scene images is a crucial task in many real-world applications like urban surveillance and management, but it is greatly challenged by the camera's perspective that causes variation in object size and shape, occlusions, and cluttered scenes. Traditional counting methods use handcrafted features and shallow models, which limit their accuracy and generalization capability. With the recent advancements in deep learning and computer vision, deep neural network-based methods have achieved state-of-the-art performance in many tasks, including crowd counting. One popular approach for crowd counting is to use convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to learn a mapping from input images to the corresponding count of people. These networks usually consist of several convolutional and pooling layers followed by fully connected layers for regression. Another approach is to use density maps, which estimate the density of people in each pixel of the input image. The density maps can then be integrated to obtain the final count. Despite the significant progress in crowd counting, there are still many challenges that need to be addressed, such as handling scale and perspective variations, occlusions, and the presence of non-person objects in the scene. Current research focuses on developing more robust and efficient deep learning models that can handle these challenges and achieving better generalization across different datasets and scenarios.

I sat nervously in the waiting room at the psychiatrist's office, fidgeting with my hands and glancing around at the other patients. Despite the fact that I'd been completely convinced for months that I was the only person left on the planet, I still couldn't help feeling like a fraud for being here. What could a shrink possibly do for someone who was, by all accounts, completely mentally sound? Still, my dwindling food supply and lack of any signs of other human life had driven me to make this appointment. As I sat there, lost in thought, the door opened and a woman in a lab coat stepped out, calling my name. "Mr. Johnson, please come in," she said with a warm smile. I followed her into the small office, where she offered me a seat and a cup of water. We talked for a while, and she asked me all the usual questions- how long had I felt this way, had I ever experienced any delusions or hallucinations, etc. I answered as honestly as I could, trying to suppress the growing feeling that this was all a waste of time. But then, she asked me something that caught me off guard. "What makes you so sure that you are the only person left on Earth, Mr. Johnson?" she asked, pen poised over her notebook. I hesitated, then gave her the same answer I always did- that I'd searched high and low for any signs of life, but had found nothing. That the world was empty, silent, and barren. She nodded as I spoke, jotting down notes. Then, suddenly, she stopped and looked up at me. "Have you considered the possibility that you might be wrong?" I stared at her, incredulous. How could she possibly suggest such a thing? I'd lived this way for months, with no food, no shelter, no hope. I'd seen nothing but ruins and emptiness. What else could there be? But as she continued to talk, her words started to sink in. Maybe there was a chance that I was mistaken. Maybe there was something I'd missed, some clue or sign that I'd overlooked in my desperation. By the time I left her office, I felt like I had a new lease on life. Maybe I wasn't the only person left after all. Maybe, just maybe, there was still hope.

The president then signs these bills into law and the budget is finalized. The process can break down if Congress cannot agree on a resolution or if they fail to pass any appropriations bills. This situation is often referred to as a "government shutdown" and it means that the government shuts down operations until the budget gets settled. Common symptoms include: tiredness poor appetite weight loss skin itching yellowing of the skin (jaundice) feeling nauseous pain in your abdomen (tummy) dark-coloured urine Diagnosis Hepatitis C is diagnosed by a blood test. If you have any unusual symptoms that make you think you might have the virus, you should see your GP or local sexual health clinic as soon as possible. If you have hepatitis C, you shouldn't donate blood or organs. You also shouldn't share needles or other injecting equipment with anyone else. Treatment If you have hepatitis C, there's a chance it could get worse over time. In some cases, it can lead to liver damage, such as cirrhosis. Most people with hepatitis C are given drug treatment to stop the virus damaging their liver. The treatment usually involves taking two or three drugs once or twice a day for 8-12 weeks. For around 80 of people, this will cure the infection. Possible side effects of the medicines used to treat hepatitis C include: tiredness feeling or being sick headaches diarrhoea loss of appetite Itching Anaemia Dizziness Rash Skin rashes can be caused by certain medications. If you are concerned about your skin, you should ask a healthcare professional Psychological side effects A small number of people taking the medication experience psychological side effects. These include: mood changes anxiety depression insomnia These side effects usually improve after treatment has ended. If you're worried about taking the drug treatment, speak to your GP, specialist or nurse beforehand. They'll be able to explain more about the possible side effects.

This work develops techniques for the sequential detection and location estimation of transient changes in the volatility (standard deviation) of time series data. In particular, we introduce a class of online algorithms for detecting changes in the volatility of time series data that are both computationally efficient and statistically robust. These algorithms use a sliding-window approach to estimate the volatility of the data, and detect changes in volatility by comparing the estimates from adjacent windows. Once a change in volatility has been detected, we also develop methods for estimating the location (i.e., time index) of the change. These methods leverage the first- and second-order moments of the data and the estimated volatilities to identify potential change points, and then refine the estimates using a segmented regression approach. The proposed algorithms are demonstrated to be effective and efficient through simulations and real-world data applications in finance and environmental monitoring. In finance, the algorithms are used to detect and locate changes in volatility for asset returns, which can aid in portfolio management and risk assessment. In environmental monitoring, the algorithms are used to detect and locate changes in air quality measurements, which can aid in identifying sources of pollution and improving public health.

Dragons have existed on Earth for as long as humans can remember, yet they have never been regarded as a threat to the human species. Instead, dragons are viewed as majestic beings that soar through the sky and stun anyone fortunate enough to catch sight of one. In the kingdom of Ferelden, life is very different than it would be without dragons. For one thing, the local villagers genuinely consider their dragons as cherished members of their community. They have learned over the years that if they look after the dragons, the dragons will, in turn, look after them. The people of Ferelden revere them, and they take great pride in building sturdy, welcoming shelters for the dragons to take refuge in when they decided to come down from the skies. The townsfolk gather to watch the dragons take flight across the fields or join in on the celebration when one is born. They understand that even the violent, seemingly enraged moments from the dragons are generally just them playing or showing their affection. Some Ferelden villagers devote their entire lives to studying dragons, learning every single detail there is to learn about their behaviours, habits, likes and dislikes. Such individuals provide insight and information to the rest of the community over time, helping them in times where they may need to approach a dragon - like when there's a chance of a hungry dragon swooping down to attack their cattle. Despite the love and appreciation of the dragons around them, life was not without its dangers. Misunderstandings could and often did occur. Ferelden was a land full of farmers, and, at times, dragons viewed them as just another food source. When this occurred, the people did not hesitate to protect themselves and their pride in a well-prepared defense team, filled with people from all communities, to face them when and if necessary. On the whole, though, the people of Ferelden were content with their world, grateful for the beauty that the dragons brought to their lives. Even with so much power at their disposal, humans had not become reckless, choosing instead to respect the creatures that shared their land, to maintain peace with them and to live harmoniously. In conclusion, Humans could learn a lot from the people of Ferelden. Dragons have been a part of life for so many years; their co-existence on equal grounds with humans is a lesson in respecting each other's worlds and cherishing the beauty of other creatures.

Hey there! The St Petersburg Paradox is a tricky math problem that asks a question about how much money you would be willing to pay to play a game. Imagine that you are playing a game where you flip a coin. If it lands on heads, you get double the amount of money that you paid to play the game. If it lands on tails, the game is over and you don't get any money. Now, the tricky part is that the amount of money you can win doubles each time you flip the coin! So, for example, if you paid 1 to play and the coin lands on heads, you win 2. But if you were playing again and the coin lands on heads, you would win 4. If it lands on heads again, you'd win 8, and so on. This is because for each node there are n-1 edges leading to other nodes, so in order to visit all nodes the algorithm must traverse all of these edges. This is because the algorithm must traverse every possible edge between two nodes in order to check if it has been visited before. Since there are n2 possible edges, the time complexity of this is O (n2). Trees: For a tree with n nodes, the average BFS search time is O (n). This is because the algorithm must traverse each node in order to visit all nodes in the tree, which takes O (n) time. The average DFS search time for a tree is O (n). We present a polynomial-space algorithm that computes the number of independent sets of any input graph in time O (1.1389 n) for graphs with maximum degree 3 and in time O (1.2594 n) for graphs with maximum degree 4, where n is the number of vertices in the graph. Our algorithm uses dynamic programming to reduce the problem of counting independent sets of a graph to the problem of counting independent sets of its subgraphs. We show that our algorithm works by analyzing the structure of graphs with maximum degree 3 and 4 and showing how they can be decomposed into smaller subgraphs. We then use a recurrence relation to compute the number of independent sets of the entire graph from the subgraphs. At the beginning of the year, OpenAI released the model-weights and code for CLIP, a model trained to determine which caption from a set of captions best fits a given image. CLIP stands for Contrastive Language-Image Pre-Training and was trained on a massive dataset of images and their associated captions. It works by embedding both the image and caption into a joint space, where the distance between the two embeddings determines the relevance of the caption to the image. One of the main applications of CLIP is for image search and retrieval. It can be used to categorize and search through large databases of images based on their associated captions or tags. Additionally, CLIP has been used for generating image descriptions and for visual question-answering tasks. Overall, CLIP is a powerful model for understanding the relationship between text and images and has a wide range of potential applications in the field of computer vision.

Torrents download in chunks, and once you've downloaded a specific chunk, you can start uploading it even if you haven't download all of the chunks. That's actually the entire reason why peer-to-peer file sharing networks exist. This is what makes the distributed nature of BitTorrent possible, and this is how it works in every single client. So if you've downloaded say half your files and then turn off uploading, everyone else will have a harder time downloading parts they don't have yet. Either way, there's no reason to not upload at the same time as you download because the whole point is to share data with others, and the more you upload, the more you can download. How do I know if I am seeding? If you look at the seeders column for a specific torrent in your BitTorrent client, you should see that the number of seeds matches the number of peers shown in the tracker. If it doesn't match, then it means that some people may not be able to download at full speed. How many seeds do I need to share a file with others? The normal number of seeds needed for a file or a torrent to work properly is usually just one. You only need one seed to distribute your file or torrent to others. But if you want to make sure others always have access to the file or torrent, you need to keep seeding for as long as others want to download them. In other words, the best practice is to continue seeding even after you've finished downloading. The more people who seed the longer a torrent will stay alive, and the faster it will download for others. Is it better to seed a single large torrent or multiple smaller ones? It is generally agreed upon by most BitTorrent users that it is better to seed a single large torrent than multiple smaller ones. This is because a single large torrent requires less resources on your computer to operate, and it also shares data with more people at once. It takes just as much effort to seed a single small torrent as it does to seed a single large torrent, but with the single large torrent you're able to help out a lot more people at the same time. What are leechers? Leechers are people who are currently downloading a file or torrent without sharing anything back to the network. While it is perfectly OK to download a file or torrent without uploading anything, it's generally frowned upon because it slows down the network. Most people tend to avoid downloading from leechers whenever possible, because it means the file or torrent will take a lot longer to download. How can I tell how many seeds and leechers a file or torrent has? For each file or torrent you download, you should see a "peers" column. Peers can be either leechers or seeders, so if you see 10 peers in the peers column, that doesn't necessarily mean 10 seeders (or 10 leechers). It just means there are 10 people sharing that file or torrent. You can view the seeder and leecher counts separately in some clients, but in others you'll just have to take a look at the ratio of seeders and leechers to figure out how many people are actually seeding. How do I stop seeding a file or torrent? You can stop seeding a file or torrent by right-clicking on it and selecting Stop Sharing, or by clicking on it and hitting the Delete button. Some clients may have different names for these options, but they all do the same thing. When you stop seeding a file or torrent, it will no longer appear in your current downloads list, or in any lists of files and torrents you're sharing. How do I delete a torrent? Deleting a torrent is different from stopping it. When you delete a torrent, everything related to it is deleted from your computer, including the files you downloaded and any .torrent files you were using. To delete a torrent, click on it and hit the Delete button. If you want to delete a torrent along with the files you downloaded, you'll need to check the box next to "delete associated data." Some clients may have different names for these options, but they all do the same thing. Can I delete a torrent without deleting the files I downloaded? Yes, you can delete a torrent without deleting the files you downloaded. To do this, right-click on the torrent and select Delete. Some clients may have different names for this option, but they all do the same thing. Once you've deleted the torrent, you can stop sharing the files you downloaded. You can do this by right-clicking on the files and selecting Stop Sharing, or by clicking on the files and hitting the Delete button. Some clients may have different names for these options, but they all do the same thing. Can I delete a file from a torrent I'm sharing? Yes, you can delete a file from a torrent you're sharing

Imagine you have a box of toys that you want to share with your friends. When your friends come over to play, you let them take one toy at a time from your box. But you don't give them the actual toys, instead you make copies of the toys and give those copies to your friends. This is kind of like what happens with a torrent download. When you start downloading a file, you are also sending out copies of the file to other people who want it. So, while you may not have finished downloading the entire file yet, you have already made and sent out some copies of what you have downloaded so far. This sharing process is called uploading, and because you are sending out copies of the file, you can end up uploading more than you have actually downloaded so far. Cool, huh?

Importance of visual context in scene understanding tasks is well recognized in the computer vision community. However, to what extent the computer vision models for image classification and semantic segmentation can benefit from the contextual information available in scene images is not fully understood. In this paper, we investigate the effectiveness of fusion-based models for exploiting visual context in the task of scene understanding. We propose a novel fusion-based framework that combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to capture both global and local contextual information in scene images. We evaluate our proposed model on three popular scene understanding tasks including image classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection. Experimental results demonstrate that our fusion-based framework significantly improves the performance of existing CNN-based models in terms of accuracy and robustness. Furthermore, our experiments show that the fused model outperforms single-stage CNN-based models as well as two-stage RNN-based models in scene understanding tasks. Our results provide strong evidence demonstrating the importance of visual context in scene understanding tasks and suggest that fusion-based models are well-suited for such applications.

What's the point of veins and arteries if there's blood all over the insides of the body already? All of that blood inside your body is in veins and arteries. Veins and arteries are vital part of our circulatory system. They are responsible for transporting blood throughout our body, bringing nutrients and oxygen to tissues and organs while removing waste and carbon dioxide in a coordinated and efficient manner. Without veins and arteries, blood would likely pool and clot inside our body leading to serious medical complications, like heart attacks or strokes. By keeping the blood in specialized vessels, the circulatory system can maintain a constant supply of oxygen and nutrients to our body's cells and organs, helping them to function in a healthy and efficient way.

The historian Frederick W. Mote wrote that the usage of the term "social classes" for this system was misleading and that the position of people within the four-class system was not static. The "internal boundaries" were not rigid, and people could move from one class to another as their economic circumstances changed. People in the lower classes were often employed in manual labor and had little or no access to education or other forms of social mobility. They lived in simple housing conditions such as huts or slums. Taking up a job in the imperial administration was a possibility for members of the upper classes. The system was abolished during the Tang dynasty, but it was later reintroduced in the Song dynasty. See also History of education in China History of poverty Citations Bibliography Fagan, Brian M.. This paper considers a network of stochastic evidence accumulators, each represented by a drift-diffusion model accruing evidence towards a decision in continuous time by observing a noisy signal and by incorporating the influence of an external control signal. The objective is to jointly optimise the input signal and the decision thresholds of all accumulators in order to maximise the overall probability of correctly discriminating between two signals. We show that the optimal solution can be found by solving a convex optimisation problem, which leads to a simple closed-form solution for the case of linear input signals. We then analyse the effect of different system parameters on the performance of the network. Finally, we provide numerical simulations which demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach. Our results demonstrate the potential of drift-diffusion models as powerful tools for optimising the performance of networks of evidence accumulators.

Fashion attribute classification is of great importance to many high-level tasks such as fashion item search, fashion trend analysis, fashion recommendation, etc. The task is challenging due to the extremely fine-grained level of the attributes and the large amount of categories. In this paper, we propose a novel end-to-end fashion attribute classification approach which is composed of two main components: a feature extraction network and an attribute classifier. The feature extraction network leverages the power of deep learning to extract high-level features from fashion images. The attribute classifier is then trained with the extracted features to classify the clothing items into different attributes. We evaluate our approach on three benchmark datasets: Fashionista, DeepFashion and DeepFashion2. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach can achieve state-of-the-art performance on these datasets.

We analyze the security of the authentication code against pollution attacks in network coding given by Oggier and Fathi and show one way to remove one very strong condition they impose to ensure security. In the paper, Oggier and Fathi present two authentication codes for use in network coding applications. They focus on the security of their codes against pollution attacks, which involve an adversary sending false messages to disrupt a network. The authors describe two conditions that must be satisfied for their codes to be secure against pollution attacks: 1) The code should be able to detect when the number of packets received is greater than or equal to some pre-defined threshold; and 2) All decodable vectors should have the same Hamming weight. To remove one very strong condition they impose to ensure security, we suggest using a variation of the authentication code proposed by Oggier and Fathi. This variation involves using a different type of code, known as a rank-metric code. Rank-metric codes are defined over finite fields and have the property that all codewords have the same rank (the sum of the ranks of its components). In the context of network coding, this can be used to detect if the number of received packets is greater than or equal to some pre-defined threshold, without imposing any restrictions on the Hamming weights of the codewords. Thus, by using a rank-metric code instead of a Hamming metric code, it is possible to remove the second condition imposed by Oggier and Fathi, while still ensuring security against pollution attacks.

Additive Animations in CSS: An Innovative Technique for Web Design Web designers and developers have a new tool in their arsenal: Additive Animations in CSS. This innovative technique allows for animations to be layered and combined in ways that were previously impossible with traditional CSS animation. With additive animations, elements on a web page can move, scale, and change colors in complex ways, creating dynamic and engaging visual effects. This technique allows for more creativity in web design, enabling designers to bring their visions to life in exciting new ways. Additive animations work by adding new rules to existing animations, creating a layered effect. This means that instead of starting from scratch for each new animation, a designer can build upon an existing animation to create more complex effects. This technique also enables designers to create more visually interesting transitions between different states of a user interface. For example, when a user clicks on a button, an additive animation might cause the button to grow larger and change color, while simultaneously causing other elements on the page to move or fade in. Additive animations in CSS are compatible across multiple browsers and devices, making them a versatile tool for web design. They can be used in a variety of contexts, from simple buttons to complex user interfaces. As web design continues to evolve, new techniques like additive animations will be crucial in creating engaging user experiences. With their flexibility and versatility, additive animations in CSS are sure to become a staple of web design for years to come.

We consider the stochastic extensible bin packing problem (SEBP) in which n items of stochastic size are packed into m bins of unit capacity. In contrast to the classical bin packing problem that has a deterministic size of items, in SEBP the size of each item is stochastic and follows a given probability distribution. The goal of the problem is to minimize the number of bins used while ensuring that all items are packed into the available bins. To achieve this, the algorithm needs to optimize the packing of the items into the bins. This can be done by using heuristics such as first-fit, best-fit, or worst-fit. Additionally, other techniques such as grouping similar items together or utilizing the memory of previous solutions can also be employed to improve the performance of the algorithm. In order to successfully solve the SEBP, it is important to consider the probability distributions of the item sizes. The selected heuristic should be able to handle the variability of the item sizes and adjust the packing strategy accordingly. Additionally, if multiple bins are available, the algorithm must be able to utilize them optimally. This can be achieved by considering the expected number of items for each bin and adjusting the packing strategy accordingly. Overall, the solution of the SEBP requires an efficient algorithm that is able to deal with the stochastic nature of the item sizes and the limited capacity of the bins. Through careful selection of heuristics and optimization techniques, the algorithm should be able to find an optimal solution in a reasonable amount of time.

In this paper, we propose a novel deep convolutional neural network (CNN) -based algorithm for solving ill-posed inverse problems. Regularized iterative algorithms have emerged as the standard approach to ill-posed inverse problems. However, these algorithms have their limitations, including slow convergence rates and sensitivity to initialization. Deep learning-based methods have shown promise in solving these issues, but most existing methods rely on fully connected layers or shallow networks. Our proposed algorithm utilizes a fully convolutional architecture, which can efficiently learn high-level information from low-level features. It also employs a residual learning framework, which speeds up convergence and enhances the stability of the algorithm. Additionally, by incorporating a skip connection into the network, our algorithm can leverage prior knowledge and improve accuracy in the reconstruction process. We tested our algorithm on several different inverse problems, including image deblurring and super-resolution, and achieved state-of-the-art performance compared to other deep learning methods and traditional iterative algorithms. Our proposed algorithm has potential applications in medical imaging, remote sensing, and computer vision.

Emergent narratives provide a unique and compelling approach to interactive storytelling through simulation, and have applications in games, narrative generation, and virtual agents. However the inherent complexity of simulation makes it challenging to create emergent narratives that are both coherent and engaging for the playeruser. One approach to addressing this challenge is to use artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques to model and understand how emergent narratives can be created and manipulated. By analyzing large amounts of data and simulating a variety of scenarios, these techniques can identify patterns and generate new narrative possibilities that are both credible and immersive. Another approach involves designing the simulation environment to provide playersusers with clear objectives and consistent rules, while still allowing for emergent narrative elements to arise organically. This can involve creating complex simulations that replicate real-world environments and events, and using game mechanics and other interactive elements to encourage player engagement and exploration. Ultimately, creating compelling emergent narratives requires a combination of innovative design, advanced technology, and a deep understanding of the human experience. As such, it remains an exciting and rapidly evolving field with numerous opportunities for creative exploration and innovation.

The composites we use are cured with blue light. NOT UV LIGHT. It is a polymerizing reaction that is initiated by (usually) camphorquinone. The polymerization is best at 470nm which is blue light. Camphorquinone is the photosensitizer that initiates the reaction. It is used because it produces a free radical which reacts with unsaturated monomers and polymers to initiate polymerization. The camphorquinone can react with oxygen in the air, which prevents it from initiating the reaction, so a tertiary amine such as ethyl 4-dimethylamino benzoate is added to the system to quench the oxygen. It is important to note that UV light is harmful to teeth and can cause yellowing of the teeth. Blue light does not have this effect.

The Rankine cycle is sometimes referred to as a practical Carnot cycle because, when an efficient turbine is used, the TS diagram begins to resemble the Carnot cycle. The main difference between the Rankine cycle and Carnot cycle is that the Carnot cycle is an idealized thermodynamic cycle, while the Rankine cycle is a practical engineering cycle. The Rankine cycle includes additional components such as pumps and boilers to increase efficiency, whereas the Carnot cycle does not. Additionally, the Rankine cycle operates on two-phase fluid, whereas the Carnot cycle operates on a single-phase gas.

This paper presents a design methodology for optimal transmission energy allocation at a sensor equipped with energy harvesting technology for remote state estimation of linear stochastic dynamical systems. In this methodology, the objective is to maximize the state estimation accuracy subject to energy constraints. The proposed approach combines a state estimator and an energy allocation policy that adaptively adjusts the transmission energy based on the available harvested energy and channel state information. The paper proposes a probabilistic approach to model and analyze the system's behavior. The proposed method takes into account the energy harvested by the sensor, the channel state information, and the estimation error covariance matrix. To optimize the energy allocation policy, the authors propose a stochastic optimization model based on the Lyapunov function approach. Simulations results show that the proposed approach achieves better estimation accuracy and energy efficiency than other state-of-the-art methods. The methodology is useful for energy-constrained wireless sensor networks, IoT applications, and smart grid systems, where energy conservation is a critical challenge. Overall, this paper contributes to the research on energy-efficient state estimation in wireless sensor networks, and it is expected to have significant practical applications in various domains.
