John had a weird soup thing. He couldn't stand the smell, the taste, or even the sight of soup. He found it repulsive and would never order it whenever he went out to eat. But despite his strong dislike of soup, he seemed to attract it wherever he went. It started off as a strange coincidence. After his first encounter with soup at a restaurant, John noticed that it kept coming back no matter where he went. No matter how hard he tried to avoid it, soup seemed to follow him everywhere. At first, he thought it was all in his head but soon enough, he realized it wasn't. Everywhere he went, someone seemed to be serving soup. It was like some kind of cosmic joke. John tried to ignore it as best as he could but it started to become an obsession. He felt like he was being haunted by soup. Whenever he walked into a restaurant, he would immediately look for the soup section on the menu. He became paranoid and started to believe that people were out to get him with soup. He even started to suspect his friends and family. Were they trying to poison him? Did they have some kind of vendetta against him? Of course, none of that was true. John was just unlucky and soup seemed to be following him around. But still, it was an odd occurrence. He wished he could figure out why this was happening. In the end, John gave up trying to understand it. He accepted that he was simply cursed with soup. He had grown accustomed to it and even started to find it amusing. He wasn't sure if he'd ever develop a liking for soup but he had stopped dreading the sight of it.

Sophie had been eagerly anticipating her first date with Chris for weeks, but as the day drew nearer, her excitement morphed into anxiety. She couldn't shake the feeling that something was going to go wrong, that she wasn't good enough for him, that they wouldn't have anything to talk about. The morning of the date, Sophie woke up with a knot in her stomach. She tried to calm herself down by listening to some calming music, but her heart was beating faster than ever before. She spent the day getting ready, fussing over every detail of her appearance. As the clock ticked closer to their meeting time, Sophie could barely contain her nerves. She paced around her apartment, wringing her hands and checking her phone every few seconds. When Chris texted to say he was running late, Sophie felt like she might burst with anxiety. Finally, he arrived at the restaurant, and Sophie's nerves reached an all-time high. But as soon as they sat down and started talking, all of her fears melted away. Chris was warm and funny and easy to talk to. They had so much in common and so much to say to each other. By the end of the night, Sophie was totally smitten. She couldn't believe how nervous and anxious she had been earlier in the day. Looking back on it, she realized that all of the worry had been for nothing. Chris was just as excited to meet her as she was to meet him, and everything had turned out perfectly in the end. From that day on, Sophie never let her nerves get the best of her again. She learned to trust herself and her ability to connect with others, and she went on to have many more wonderful dates with Chris and others. But she always remembered the lesson that her first nervous date had taught her: that sometimes, the things we worry about the most never come to pass, and that it's always worth taking a chance on love.

Possible newsflash: America's First DAO Approved in Wyoming In a historic move, the state of Wyoming has granted legal recognition to America's first decentralized autonomous organization (DAO), signaling a new era of innovation and experimentation in digital finance and governance. The DAO, called the American CryptoFed DAO, is a non-profit entity that uses blockchain technology to create a new type of digital currency, called the DAC, that is backed by a basket of stable assets and can be used for peer-to-peer payments and other financial transactions without intermediaries. To gain approval from the Wyoming authorities, the American CryptoFed DAO had to comply with various regulatory requirements and prove its technical and operational competence, as well as its commitment to transparency and investor protection. According to the DAO's co-founder, Marian Orr, who is also the former mayor of Cheyenne, Wyoming, "This is a historic day for blockchain technology and for Wyoming. We are proud to be the first DAO in America and to show the world what is possible when you combine innovation, cooperation, and regulation in a positive way." The approval of the American CryptoFed DAO is seen as a major boost for the blockchain and crypto industry, as it opens up new avenues for fundraising, investing, and community building that could challenge traditional models of finance and governance. Some experts believe that DAOs could eventually become the dominant form of organization in many fields, from healthcare to education to entertainment, by allowing people to collaborate and coordinate their efforts in a decentralized and transparent way. However, DAOs also face many challenges and risks, such as governance disputes, technical vulnerabilities, and regulatory uncertainties, that need to be addressed for them to achieve their full potential. Nevertheless, the approval of America's first DAO in Wyoming is a bold step towards a more decentralized and democratic future, where individuals can have more control over their assets, their data, and their communities.

While some may argue that doping should be accepted in professional sports and the Olympics as it allows athletes to reach new heights and push the limits of human capabilities, there are several reasons why this position is problematic. Firstly, doping places the health and well-being of athletes at risk, as it often involves the use of harmful and potentially life-threatening substances. Furthermore, allowing doping would create an uneven playing field, as not all athletes have access to the same resources or are willing to risk their health. This could lead to a situation where only those who are willing to cheat are able to succeed, while the integrity of the competition is compromised. Additionally, allowing doping would undermine the spirit of fair play and competition that is central to sportsmanship and the Olympic ideals. Overall, while it may be tempting to accept doping as a means of achieving greater athletic performance, the risks and negative consequences far outweigh any potential benefits.

Snap, the parent company of Snapchat, has just announced the acquisition of a brain-computer interface startup called CTRL-Labs. The deal is reportedly worth around 1 billion and will be used to develop augmented reality (AR) glasses for Snap in the future. CTRL-Labs was founded in 2015 by Thomas Reardon and Patrick Kaifosh, both former Microsoft engineers. The startup specialized in creating AR experiences that utilized brain signals as input. This technology could allow users to control digital objects with their thoughts, rather than having to use physical devices like keyboards or touchscreens. Snap's CEO, Evan Spiegel, said the acquisition was an exciting opportunity to explore how this technology could be used to enhance the user experience of its products. He believes CTRL-Labs' technology could be used to create a more natural way to interact with devices. "We believe that integrating these technologies into our products will allow us to create even more engaging and immersive experiences for our users," Spiegel said in a statement. The acquisition of CTRL-Labs is a major step forward for Snap in its ambitions to launch its own line of AR glasses. It is not yet clear when the glasses will be released, but it is likely that the technology from CTRL-Labs will play a big role in the design and development of the product. This acquisition is one in a series of moves made by Snap to diversify its product lineup. Last year, the company released its first hardware product, Spectacles 3, which featured two cameras and allowed users to take 3D photos and videos.

Once upon a time, deep in a faraway forest, there was a young boy named Lucas. He had always been fascinated with magic, and spent countless hours practicing card tricks and sleight of hand. One day, as Lucas was walking through the forest, he came across a clearing. As he approached, he saw a magnificent tent set up in the center. A sign read "The Great Zoltar's Magic Show - Tonight Only!" Lucas could hardly believe his luck. He had heard of the Great Zoltar, one of the greatest magicians in the world. With a quick glance around to make sure nobody was watching, Lucas sneaked into the tent and found a seat in the back. As the show began, Lucas was mesmerized by Zoltar's incredible illusions. The magician pulled rabbits out of hats, made doves appear out of thin air, and even levitated above the stage. Lucas had never seen anything like it. But then, towards the end of the show, something truly amazing happened. Zoltar announced that he was going to perform his most daring trick yet, one that he had never before attempted in public. With a wave of his wand, he made a giant crystal ball appear. Zoltar asked for a volunteer from the audience, and Lucas eagerly raised his hand. He was chosen to come up on stage and help with the trick. Zoltar asked Lucas to place his hands on the crystal ball and say a magic word. As soon as Lucas did so, the ball began to glow with a bright light. Suddenly, Lucas felt himself being lifted off the ground. He was floating! Higher and higher he went, until he was soaring above the treetops. Lucas looked down and saw the entire forest spread out beneath him. It was the most incredible feeling he had ever experienced. And then, just as suddenly as it had begun, the magic ended. Lucas was back on the stage, surrounded by applause. As the show ended and the audience began to leave, Lucas approached Zoltar and asked how he had done the trick. But Zoltar simply smiled and said, "A magician never reveals his secrets." From that day on, Lucas knew that he too wanted to be a magician. He spent years practicing and perfecting his craft, until one day he too became known as the Great Lucas. And whenever he performed, he always remembered the magic show that had inspired him to embark on his own magical journey.

There are several counter-arguments that can be made to refute the opinion that rock music is no longer culturally relevant. While it may not be as dominant in the mainstream as it once was, there are still numerous rock acts that are hugely successful, both commercially and critically. Bands like Foo Fighters, Radiohead, and Arcade Fire continue to release celebrated albums and sell out arenas around the world. Furthermore, rock music has played a significant role in shaping popular culture over the past several decades. It has been a driving force behind numerous social and political movements, and has been instrumental in shaping youth culture in the United States and abroad. The genre has also spawned countless sub-genres and continues to evolve, with bands incorporating elements of electronic music, hip-hop, and other genres to create new and exciting sounds. Ultimately, the idea that rock music is no longer culturally relevant is simply untrue. While it may not be as dominant in the mainstream as it once was, the genre continues to thrive and evolve, and its impact on popular culture is significant and enduring.

The Reddit post argues that people who say victims of suicide are selfish are actually the ones who are selfish. However, this argument is flawed for several reasons. First, it assumes that all people who commit suicide are victims. This is not always the case; sometimes people who commit suicide are doing so because they are in pain and want to end their suffering. Second, the argument conflates selfishness with self-centeredness. While selfishness can be a form of self-centeredness, the two are not synonymous. Selfishness implies a lack of concern for others, while self-centeredness simply means that someone is focused on their own needs and wants. Finally, the argument fails to consider that people who are suicidal may not be thinking clearly and may not be able to see beyond their own pain. It gets onto your computer when you open an email attachment or click on a bad link, and then it starts spreading to other computers that are connected to yours. The Basal Eurasians are thought to be descended from an ancient population that lived in what is now Siberia and migrated westward and southward during the last Ice Age. The team of international researchers used genomic data from more than 1,500 individuals from around the world to trace the genetic contributions of different populations to modern Europeans. They found that the Basal Eurasian ancestry made up between 5-10 of the genomes of modern Europeans. This makes it the fourth most significant ancestral source of DNA in Europeans, after the Near Eastern farmers, hunter-gatherers from the Paleolithic period and a mysterious population known as the "Ancient North Eurasians." The findings suggest that the Basal Eurasians intermingled with other populations in Europe after the Ice Age, likely playing a role in the development of different regional cultures. The team also found evidence that some Basal Eurasian ancestry may have been introduced to Europe by migrations from the East in more recent times. The discovery of this previously unknown ancestral group highlights the complexity of the human story, and the importance of studying our genetic history in order to better understand our current diversity.

The first state is a spin-polarized metal, which means that the electrons in the graphene layers all have the same spin orientation. This is significant because it could lead to the creation of new spintronic devices that use the spin of electrons to transmit information. The second state is a quantum spin Hall insulator, which is a material that is insulating in the bulk but conducts electricity on its edges. This finding could also lead to the development of new electronic devices, such as spin-based transistors and logic gates. Overall, this discovery has opened up a new field in condensed matter physics and could revolutionize the way we think about electronic devices. Further research will be needed to fully understand these new quantum states and how they can be used in real-world applications.

At first, people were apprehensive about the tests and how they would be used to separate them. But as time passed, most people accepted their fate and moved to their designated zones. The zones were vastly different from one another, with the highest zone providing its citizens with all the comforts of life, while the lowest zone was a slum filled with poverty and crime. Some people tried to cross between zones, either for better opportunities or just for curiosity's sake, but the border guards were strict and rarely allowed anyone through. For the most part, people settled into a routine and lived according to their scores. The higher one's score, the better their quality of life. But no matter where a person's score placed them, everyone was held accountable to the same laws and regulations that applied to all of humanity. The Goodness Test changed the way the world worked, but it also brought peace and understanding to many who had previously been at odds with one another. It was a reminder that no matter one's score, everyone was still human and deserved respect.

Tesla read many works, memorizing complete books, and supposedly possessed a photographic memory.:33 He was a polyglot, speaking eight languages: Serbo-Croatian, Czech, English, French, German, Hungarian, Italian, and Latin.:282 Tesla became a naturalized citizen of the United States in 1891.:33 He developed a lifelong rivalry with Thomas Edison, who promoted direct current (DC) for electric power distribution over alternating current (AC). Tesla's alternating current (AC) induction motor and related polyphase AC patents, licensed by Westinghouse Electric in 1888, earned him a considerable amount of money and formed the cornerstone of the polyphase system which that company would eventually market. Attempts to develop a commercial motor were thwarted by business rivals, particularly Edison supporters, who succeeded in defeating his attempt to obtain an alternating current construction patent in New York. In 1893, Tesla tried to interest American financier J. P. Morgan in financing an "AC motor" project, intending to develop it with help from French firm Leroy-Beaulieu. Although Morgan initially agreed to finance the project, he turned down Tesla's request for more money to construct a wireless telecommunications tower and laboratory, known as Wardenclyffe. In 1895, Tesla constructed a demonstration wireless transmitter and receiver called the "Tesla coil," capable of producing low-frequency long-distance radio waves. During this time, Tesla worked on a number of ideas that he never brought to fruition. These included: a bladeless turbine, or the "Tesla turbine," based on the boundary layer effect; dynamo-electric machines, or alternators, using the principals of rotating magnetic fields to produce alternating current; a magnetic field theory of gravity, attempting to explain gravitation as a result of a static magnetic field; a teleforce weapon, or death ray, which was never completed but motivation for its construction is unclear, although Tesla did say that such a weapon could "bring down a fleet of 10,000 enemy airplanes at a distance of 200 miles"; and a proposal to transmit electrical energy without wires, based on the concept of electrical conduction through the Earth itself. Tesla died poor and living alone in New York City on January 7, 1943, at the age of 86, having been in failing health since at least 1931. In 1999, Time magazine named Tesla one of the 100 most influential people of the 20th century.

The function of the chloroplast is to convert light energy into chemical energy that can be used by plants to create glucose from carbon dioxide and water in a process called photosynthesis. Lena had always been a wanderer, a lover of adventure, and an explorer at heart. She had always made plans to travel the world and see all the beautiful places it had to offer. But when Lena got the news that she had been diagnosed with cancer, all her dreams of seeing the world came to a sudden halt. For two years, Lena's life had shifted to hospital visits, chemotherapy treatments, and the unbearable fatigue that followed. The long battle had pushed her to her limits, and she had lost all hope of ever travelling again. One day, when Lena was feeling a little better than usual, she decided to take a long walk around her neighborhood. She strolled slowly, taking in the fresh air, and enjoying the sunshine. She noticed how beautiful the trees looked, how the breeze felt on her skin, and how glad she was to be out of bed on this lovely day. As she walked, Lena began to imagine herself traveling the world, seeing all the places she had always dreamed of seeing, and doing all the things she had always wanted to do. She imagined herself climbing mountains, swimming in the ocean, and experiencing different cultures. By the time Lena had made it back home, something had clicked inside her. She realized that she didn't need to travel to other countries to have an adventure. She could have adventures in her own backyard. All she had to do was go out and explore, and see the world around her with new eyes. From that day on, Lena started going on longer and longer walks. She would walk through the town, then the nearby forests and fields. She found beauty in the simplest of things that she had never noticed before, and her sense of adventure returned to her once more. With each passing day, Lena grew stronger, taking on longer walks, and even running some days. Her last scan showed no signs of cancer, and Lena knew it was all because of the long walks she had started to take. Her journey had started with a step, just like any other journey. But the long walk had led her to a path of healing, discovery, and a renewed love of life. Lena realized that the longest journey is often the one inside of ourselves and that there's always something to be discovered when we open our eyes and take a closer look at the world around us.

According to scholars Walter Kramer, Gotz Trenkler, Gerhard Ritter, and Gerhard Prause, the story of the posting on the door, even though it has settled as one of the pillars of the Protestant Reformation, may not have happened exactly as popular tradition would have it. While Martin Luther almost certainly did write and submit his 95 Theses to the church authorities, it is unlikely that he actually posted them on the door of the Castle Church in Wittenberg. Instead, these scholars suggest that Luther may have simply sent the document to Archbishop Albrecht of Mainz and to other church leaders in order to spark discussion and debate about the sale of indulgences, which was one of the primary issues he was seeking to address. Regardless of the specific details of how the 95 Theses were disseminated, however, there is no doubt that they had a profound impact on the religious landscape of Europe and played a significant role in the Protestant Reformation.

The Intensive Care Unit (ICU) is a hospital department where machine learning has the potential to provide valuable assistance in clinical decision making. Classical machine learning models usually only provide a single prediction, which in many cases makes them unsuitable for ICU settings. In this paper, we propose a new method for multi-output prediction in the ICU using deep learning. Our model is based on a recurrent neural network (RNN) with long short-term memory cells (LSTMs). We train the model on data from the MIMIC-III database, and use it to predict six different clinical variables: heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, urine output, and Glasgow Coma Scale score. We found that our model outperforms existing methods for multi-output prediction in the ICU. In particular, our model is able to make accurate predictions for all six clinical variables, even when the input data is limited.

One possible counter-argument to refute the opinion that IDs should be required to vote is that such a requirement could disproportionately disenfranchise certain groups of people, particularly those who face barriers to obtaining government-issued ID, such as low-income individuals, elderly people, people with disabilities, and members of minority groups. In some cases, obtaining an ID can be costly, time-consuming, or difficult due to transportation barriers or lack of access to necessary documents. Additionally, the problem of voter fraud, which voter ID laws are intended to address, is actually quite rare in the United States; according to a study by the Brennan Center for Justice, the incidence of in-person voter fraud is between 0.00004 and 0.0009. Therefore, the burden of requiring everyone to obtain an ID in order to vote may outweigh the potential benefits of preventing this exceedingly rare form of fraud. Finally, it is worth noting that voter ID laws have been found to have a disproportionate impact on certain populations, particularly Black and Latino communities. While the specific impact of these laws varies depending on how they are designed and implemented, it is clear that they can have a negative impact on voting rights and should be approached with caution to ensure that they do not unfairly disenfranchise any group of voters.

Passengers Escaped Smoke-Filled Plane by Jumping from Wing After Electrical Fault Causes Problems, Investigators Report Travellers on board a flight from Dubai to Lahore had to make an emergency exit after an electrical fault caused a series of problems, filling the cabin with smoke. According to investigators, passengers on the Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) Boeing 777 were forced to exit the plane via its wing. The incident occurred on Friday, shortly after the plane took off from Dubai when it suffered an electrical fault. Passengers then reported smelling smoke and burning wires. The plane diverted to Karachi where it landed safely, but not before passengers were forced to evacuate by jumping from the wing. PIA officials reported that all passengers were safely evacuated and there were no injuries. The cause of the electrical fault is still being investigated by authorities. "The safety and security of our passengers is our top priority," said a statement from PIA. "We are conducting a thorough investigation into the incident and are working closely with authorities to ensure that such an incident does not happen again in the future." This is not the first incident involving PIA this year. In May, a PIA flight crashed in a residential area near Karachi airport, resulting in the death of 97 people. The cause of that incident is also still under investigation. The latest incident again raises concerns over flight safety and the need for airlines to ensure that their planes are properly maintained and equipped to handle emergencies. It is hoped that the investigation will shed more light on the cause of the electrical fault and that appropriate measures will be taken to prevent such incidents from happening in the future.

Government limits to teachers' pay and "real terms cuts" to school budgets risk undermining standards, they warn. "Teachers need a pay rise," they urge, in a joint statement to the government. Despite the promises made by the Government that education would be 'fully-funded', school budgets have been subject to real terms cuts for almost a decade. Oil prices plummeted to their lowest levels since 2009 as global production remains high and the demand for oil continues to remain low. The benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) fell to 33.45 per barrel on Tuesday, its lowest level since February 2009. This is a fraction of the more than 100 per barrel price that oil fetched back in 2014. Analysts attribute this sharp decline to the coronavirus pandemic, which has caused a significant drop in global demand for oil. With fewer cars, planes and ships in use, there is less need for fuel. In addition, OPEC countries have kept production levels relatively high despite the decreased demand, further driving down the price. This situation is likely to remain for some time. Many countries are still taking steps to limit the spread of COVID-19, such as travel restrictions, which will likely continue to adversely affect the demand for oil. For now, oil producers who rely heavily on oil revenue are feeling the pinch. Smaller countries, such as Venezuela and Nigeria, are particularly vulnerable. It remains to be seen how long oil prices will stay at these low levels. But if demand doesn't pick up soon, it could mean major consequences for the global economy.

From video streaming to security and surveillance applications, video data play an important role in our daily living today. However, managing a large amount of video data and retrieving the relevant information from it is challenging. As video data often contains high-dimensional features, traditional retrieval techniques are not efficient or accurate enough for large-scale video datasets. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel deep learning-based end-to-end video retrieval framework, which consists of two main components: a feature extraction module and a retrieval module. The feature extraction module utilizes convolutional neural networks to extract high-level semantic features from video frames, while the retrieval module uses a multi-layer perceptron to map the extracted features into a semantic space and then perform retrieval based on content similarity. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Additionally, we provide extensive ablation studies to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed network architectures.

A defence official said in a statement on Wednesday that its nuclear programme had "long been in the full-fledged stage of miniaturisation." However, analysts say while there is evidence the North has shrunk the size of its weapons, whether it has achieved miniaturisation is unclear. North Korea's announcement came as South Korean troops were involved in a gun battle with the North - killing two soldiers and wounding at least one other - after they crossed the tense border to chase a defector. The incident occurred on Tuesday during an exercise south of the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) that divides the peninsula. North Korea said the soldiers had "fired shots at our side" while the defectors were being chased. A statement released by Pyongyang's state news agency KCNA said the soldiers "rudely shot dead two of our people who were running toward the [South] for dear life." It also accused the South of "deliberately provoking" the North by firing across the DMZ with K-2 rifles. Seoul insists it did not fire at the soldiers, saying that their weapons only fire blanks. 'Attention-grabbing gimmick' The incident comes amid heightened tensions between the two sides. Last month, North Korea launched what it said was a new intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM), which it claimed could reach anywhere in the US. The launch, which violated UN Security Council resolutions, sparked international condemnation. The North's leader Kim Jong-un has said that his country is close to completing its nuclear programme, which he believes will protect the North from a US invasion. The Trump administration has called the North's nuclear ambitions "unacceptable," and the White House has refused to rule out a military option. US Secretary of State Rex Tillerson has been trying to persuade China, North Korea's closest ally, to intervene, but Beijing has so far refused to put significant pressure on Pyongyang. Beijing has instead urged Washington and Seoul to stop hosting joint military drills and cancel the deployment of the THAAD anti-missile system in the South. The US media has also raised concerns about Mr Trump's ability to handle the crisis, with some critics describing him as unstable, impulsive and unprepared. Image copyright Reuters Image caption North Korea's leader Kim Jong-un has said that his country is close to completing its nuclear programme North Korea's latest claim about miniaturising nuclear warheads has been met with scepticism by analysts. "I think this is just another attention-grabbing gimmick," Andrei Lankov, a North Korea expert from Kookmin University, told the BBC. "This is not the first time that we hear such claims, but I believe they are exaggerated, or prematurely announced." He added that it may be aimed at increasing North Korea's bargaining power ahead of future talks with the US. "They want to create the impression that they are an invincible nuclear power, when in fact they are still not a real nuclear power."

Wireless communications are vulnerable against radio frequency (RF) jamming which might be caused either intentionally or unintentionally. A particular subset of wireless networks, vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANET) which incorporate a large number of vehicles, are particularly vulnerable to jamming. In a VANET, the vehicles communicate with each other to share information about the road conditions, traffic, accidents and road blocks etc. The data is exchanged between vehicles and Road Side Units (RSUs) located along the roads to facilitate safer driving. There are many different approaches proposed by researchers to mitigate the effects of jamming. Some of the techniques involve identifying the jamming source and its location. Other methods try to reduce the effect of the jamming attack by changing the transmission parameters of the nodes e.g., frequency, power, time and space. These methods use specific assumptions about the network characteristics and the type of jammer. For example, the jammer may be located near the sender (s), or the attacker may have some control over the frequencies used, the transmit power, etc. Another approach is to use cryptography to encrypt the communication between the sender and receiver. However, this approach has the disadvantage that it requires a shared secret key between the sender and receiver. Finally, another method is to employ collaborative diversity in which multiple nodes cooperate to create an effective reception at the destination. In this paper, we propose a new collaborative diversity technique to reduce the effect of jamming attacks in VANETs. Our technique is motivated by the fact that, in a VANET, the nodes can be arranged in different road segments. The nodes in one segment can cooperate to form a virtual antenna array which can receive the signal from the neighboring segment. The nodes in the neighboring segment can then decode the signal by using Maximum Likelihood (ML) detection. We show that our technique can effectively reduce the effect of jamming attacks in VANETs.

The Rankine cycle is the fundamental thermodynamic underpinning of the steam engine. The cycle is an arrangement of components as is typically used for simple power production, and utilizes the working fluid of water or steam. The Rankine cycle describes the process of converting thermal energy into mechanical work, which can be used to generate electricity. The components of the Rankine cycle include a boiler to convert water into steam, a turbine to extract mechanical work from the steam, a condenser to condense the steam back into water, and a pump to return the water to the boiler. The cycle operates on the principle of a heat engine, where heat energy is absorbed at high temperature, and then rejected at low temperature. The Rankine cycle can be analyzed using thermodynamic principles to determine its efficiency, which is the ratio of the net work output to the heat input. The efficiency of the cycle is strongly influenced by the operating parameters of the system, such as the pressure and temperature at which the steam is produced in the boiler and the temperature at which it is condensed in the condenser. Overall, the Rankine cycle is a key concept in the development of steam power and has been used for decades as a means of generating power in large-scale power plants, as well as in smaller applications such as heating systems and steam turbines.

Both acids and bases can cause burns to the skin by reacting with and damaging the skin's tissues. The severity of the burn depends on the concentration and amount of the acid or base that comes into contact with the skin. Acids typically release hydrogen ions (H) when they come in contact with water, which can then penetrate the skin and react with molecules in the skin's tissues. This reaction can break down cellular structures, damage proteins, and cause tissue death, leading to skin burns. Bases, on the other hand, release hydroxide ions (OH when they come into contact with water, which can also penetrate the skin and react with molecules in the skin's tissues. This reaction can cause a similar breakdown of cellular structures and damage to proteins, leading to skin burns. In summary, both acids and bases cause burns to the skin by reacting with and damaging the skin's tissues at a chemical level through the release of ions.

Engineering giant Bosch is currently spearheading a new development - "textured" touchscreens that are designed to be fitted into the next generation of automobiles. These touchscreens are expected to drastically improve the user experience when compared to flat, conventional touchscreens. Bosch developed the technology that utilizes haptic feedback to simulate the physical sensation of a button being pressed, even though the touchscreen is flat. This new development is expected to enhance drivers' ability to use the touchscreen while keeping their eyes on the road. By using textured surfaces on the touchscreen, the driver is provided with tactile feedback from the display, and this enables them to experience the sensation of touching and pressing mechanical buttons. In addition, the technology can also be used to relay warnings, alerts, or other critical information. The use of advanced touchscreen technology in automobiles is not new. However, Bosch's innovation takes the technology further by incorporating a tangible texture on the surface of the screen. This texture provides drivers with a physical and tactile reference point to locate buttons without needing to turn their attention away from the screen or take their eyes off the road. Bosch is seen as a leader in the automotive industry when it comes to technology development. Growing up, my friends and I loved playing tag. We would spend our afternoons running around the park, laughing and chasing each other. But there was always one problem - I was never able to tag anyone. No matter how fast or sneaky I was, my friends would always find a way to evade me. And so, I remained "it" for years to come, through middle school and high school, and even beyond. As we grew older and went off to college, we lost touch with each other. It was one of my childhood friends, and we immediately fell into conversation as if no time had passed. Before I knew it, we were all there - all my old friends from the game of tag, gathered together in one place. It was as if we were still kids, and the game was about to begin. I knew that this was my moment - my chance to finally tag someone else and rid myself of this childhood curse. My heart raced as we counted down, and as soon as the game began, I took off, determined to tag my first victim. My friends were just as fast as I remembered, but this time, I was wiser. I anticipated their moves, I used their weaknesses against them. And slowly but surely, I tagged one after the other. Each time, I could feel a weight lifting off my shoulders. I was no longer "it" - I was finally free. As the game ended and we all said our goodbyes, I felt a sense of closure. The game of tag may have held me captive for years, but finally, I was able to break free from it. And as I walked away, I knew that I would always cherish this moment - the moment when I finally caught up to my childhood friends and left the game of tag behind.

It had already suffered tremendous losses in the first World War, and the second World War only added to the destruction. In addition, the death toll of the Soviet Union was horrific - estimates suggest that roughly twice as many people died in the Soviet Union than in any other country during the war. The loss of life, as well as the destruction of infrastructure and resources, meant that the US and UK were unable to recover quickly or effectively from the war. The same could be said of the Soviet Union, which experienced decades of hardship and strife following the war. In the end, all three countries paid a heavy price for their involvement in the war, and none of them truly emerged as winners.

An Australian mother has been found to be suffering from "forgotten baby syndrome" after her young son died in a hot car, an inquest has heard. The woman, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was caring for her two children at home when the tragedy occurred in April 2019. The inquest heard that the father of the children had gone out and the mother had put her son in his car seat and forgotten him, believing the father had taken him with him. The mother realised what had happened when she went to pick up her son from daycare and found he was not there. She then rushed back home and discovered his lifeless body in the car. The coroner's report said the mother suffered from "forgotten baby syndrome," a condition where parents unintentionally and temporarily forget about their child in a vehicle. In his findings, the coroner said the mother was obviously devastated by the death of her son, but that it was clear she had not intended for him to die in the car. He said that while the mother should have taken greater care to ensure her son's safety, the incident was the result of a tragic mistake. The coroner has now recommended that parents be educated on the risks associated with leaving children unattended in cars. He has also called for better public awareness campaigns to ensure that such tragedies are prevented in the future.

I awoke with a start and a feeling of dread. I was sure I had just heard something outside my window; a low, guttural moan that sent chills down my spine. I cautiously stepped out of bed, checking to make sure the door was locked before peering out into the darkness. My heart sank when I saw him there, standing in the shadows of my front porch. He was tall and thin, with long, gangly limbs and a face shrouded by a tattered hood. I couldn't see his eyes, but I could feel them staring right at me. I stumbled back, fumbling for the phone as I backed away. I dialed 911, but all I heard was static on the other end. I slammed the phone down, my mind racing. What was this thing? Why was it here? As I watched, it slowly reached out its hand, pointing directly at me. I felt my knees go weak as I saw what was in its grasp - my favorite glass of Kool-Aid! I'd left it on the windowsill earlier that day, and now this...thing had taken it. I watched, paralyzed with fear, as it took a sip from my glass. I felt violated and disgusted, wondering how it even knew I liked Kool-Aid. Then, with one last look at me, it turned and disappeared into the night. I never saw it again, but I learned an important lesson that night: never leave your Kool-Aid unattended.

His poor physical health made him short-tempered and even harsher in his writings and comments. His wife Katharina was overheard saying, "Dear husband, you are too rude," and he responded, "Be quiet, woman; you are not a man." His works included The Birth of Tragedy (1872), Beyond Good and Evil (1886), On the Genealogy of Morals (1887) and Ecce Homo (1888). He also wrote numerous plays and essays. In his last months he decided to retire to Weimar, where he died at the age of 55. What did the critics say? Friedrich Nietzsche is one of the most widely read philosophers in the world. The German philosopher was born on October 15, 1844 He died aged 55 in Weimar in 1900 Nietzsche's ideas have impacted on fields such as philosophy, psychoanalysis, sociology, politics, literature and arts In his final days he suffered from severe delirium and paralysis "The Birth of Tragedy" is often considered to be his first major work He is known for his saying "God is dead." He believed that Christian morality oppressed humanity by demanding self-denial and making us ashamed of our natural desires He thought this morality would lead to the self-destructive dialects of nihilism and nihilism He also coined the phrase: "That which does not kill us makes us stronger" A controversial figure, Nietzsche has been linked with both far-right and far-left movements Charles Darwin once described Nietzsche as "the most deep and original thinker in Europe." Indeed, some reviewers thought The Birth of Tragedy had turned upside down the whole history of philosophy. Others said it was the product of a "deranged brain." In Beyond Good and Evil and other works, Nietzsche's main focus was on the revaluation of values. Some critics said his passion for irony and aphorisms made him difficult to understand. Others saw him as a master of rhetoric and argued that he used language to mask the fact that his arguments were often contradictory. What impact did he have on society? Nietzsche's ideas had a profound impact on many writers and thinkers, including George Bernard Shaw, James Joyce, Marcel Proust, Jean-Paul Sartre, Michel Foucault, Gilles Deleuze, Edward Said, Salman Rushdie, Arundhati Roy, Susan Sontag, Wolfram von Eschenbach, Thomas Mann, Erich Fromm, Oscar Wilde, Thomas Mann and Franz Kafka. His ideas were also influential in the development of existentialism, post-modernism, deconstruction and psychotherapy. However, his ideas have also been taken up by far-right and fascist movements. I disagree that the current issue of same-sex marriage is todays equivalent to the interracial marriage issue of the 1960's and prior. Although both issues involve questions of discrimination, the legal and social implications of same-sex marriage are much more complex than those of interracial marriage. Issues such as adoption rights, co-parenting rights, marriage benefits, and religious recognition are unique to same-sex marriage and do not apply to interracial couples, making the two issues fundamentally different. Additionally, while interracial marriage was historically banned in many states, same-sex marriage has never been explicitly barred by law. Therefore, while both issues may be controversial, they are not truly comparable.

Finally, the day was over, and the students went home, exhausted and mentally drained. Days turned into weeks, and the whole town was waiting for the results. Finally, the day arrived, and the school announced the scores. Everyone was on edge, waiting to hear who had made it to the top ten. President-elect Donald Trump has announced his choice for US ambassador to the United Nations: South Carolina Governor Nikki Haley. Haley, a Republican and a former critic of Trump, was praised by the president-elect as a "proven dealmaker" who will represent the United States with great distinction. Haley, who is the daughter of Indian immigrants and the first woman to be elected governor of South Carolina, has been a rising star in Republican politics for several years. She gained national attention in 2015 when she led a successful campaign to have the Confederate flag removed from the state capitol after a gunman killed nine black parishioners in a Charleston church. Despite their past disagreements, Trump said that he and Haley had developed a strong relationship in recent weeks. "She's done an amazing job as governor of South Carolina, and we're very proud of her. She's a very talented governor, great talent, and we know she will be an outstanding ambassador to the United Nations," Trump said. Haley's nomination will now be subject to confirmation by the US Senate. If approved, she will assume one of the country's most high-profile diplomatic positions, representing the US at the world body that oversees global issues such as peace and security, human rights, and international development. Trump's choice of Haley as ambassador to the UN suggests that he is looking to diversify his cabinet and administration. Haley, who is of Indian descent, would report directly to Secretary of State nominee Rex Tillerson and work alongside other high-ranking officials like Defense Secretary nominee James Mattis and National Security Adviser nominee Michael Flynn. Haley's selection also echoes the president-elect's promise to shake up Washington and bring fresh perspectives to government. If confirmed, Haley would bring a much-needed outsider's view to the United Nations, a body that is often criticized for being bureaucratic and elitist. For her part, Haley said she was honored by the opportunity to serve her country on the world stage. "When the president-elect asked if I would serve as our ambassador to the United Nations, I was humbled. And when we discussed it further, I became convinced that the opportunity to serve with such talented and dedicated public servants was something I had to take on," she said in a statement. With Haley's nomination, Trump continues to assemble his team of advisers, officials, and ambassadors. As he moves forward with his transition to the presidency, the world will be watching closely to see how his choices shape the future of the United States and its relations with other nations.

In a breakthrough study, Stanford researchers have discovered an easier and faster way to create diamonds - one that effectively "cheats" the thermodynamics of the process. The research team found that they could use microwaves to drastically reduce the time required to turn graphite into diamonds. It typically takes days or weeks for diamond formation through conventional methods; with microwaves, it only takes minutes. The team proved their method by placing graphite in a microwave cavity, where microwaves heat and pressurize it until a diamond forms. They also cross-checked their results using traditional high-pressure, high-temperature (HPHT) equipment. The microwaves were able to achieve the same effect as HPHT in a fraction of the time. Lead researcher Dr. John McLean was stunned by the finding. "We initially weren't sure if this would even work," he said. "But we were amazed to find that we could produce diamonds in such a short amount of time. We're essentially cheating the thermodynamics of diamond production." This discovery could have far-reaching implications for industries that rely on diamonds, such as the jewelry industry. It could make diamonds much more accessible and cheaper to produce, allowing them to be used in more applications. The study has been published in the journal Nature Communications. Now, researchers fromOhio State University have found that when two layers of graphene are assembled into a double-layer stack, the proximity produces quantum states that have never been observed before. These states are an example of two-dimensional topological insulators. Topological insulators are materials with an insulating interior but conducting electrons on their surface. The conducting surface states are protected against backscattering by time reversal symmetry. In the past few years, there has been much interest in these materials because they could be used to create more efficient semiconductors. In addition, topological insulators may find applications in spintronics and quantum computing. The new Ohio State research shows that when two layers of graphene are assembled into a double-layer stack, they form a giant Dirac cone. This cone is distinguished by its unusual band structure that resembles a cone with a flat top. The scientists say that this Dirac cone is the biggest one ever observed. "We have found a novel quantum state of matter in which electrons behave like massless particles that travel at very high speed, yet have insulating properties," said researcher Yuanbo Zhang, who led the study. Public Health England (PHE) has published a review that suggests introducing a minimum price per unit of alcohol in England would have a positive impact on heavy drinkers' health. The review argues that if the proposal is implemented, it could help reduce the number of hospital admissions, save public money and improve the overall wellbeing of the country's heaviest drinkers. According to the PHE review, setting a minimum price of 50p per unit of alcohol would have the greatest benefit for those consuming more than 14 units a week, who are at greater risk of developing health problems such as liver disease, cancer and mental health issues. The report adds that it would also help address the burden on the NHS, as approximately 1.2 million hospital admissions per year are related to alcohol, with a cost of 3.5bn to the NHS and wider society. The PHE review also suggests that introducing a minimum price for alcohol could help to reduce health inequalities, as it would have a more significant impact on people from lower socio-economic backgrounds who are disproportionately affected by the harmful effects of alcohol. The review highlights that although there may be initial concerns around the impact on lower-income households, PHE believes that the policy would only have a negligible impact on moderate drinkers and would help them to save money by avoiding cheap, high-strength alcohol. Colin Shevills, Director of Balance, the North East Alcohol Office, has welcomed the review's findings, stating that "a minimum unit price would be a powerful measure to protect the most vulnerable in our society." He argues that "drinking large quantities of cheap, high-strength alcohol is a real problem in the north-east of England, where we have some of England's poorest communities." The review has also been welcomed by the Scottish government, who have already implemented a minimum price per unit of alcohol in Scotland, a move that has been credited with reducing alcohol harm since its introduction in 2018. Overall, the review presents a compelling case for the implementation of a minimum price per unit of alcohol in England. By reducing the burden on the NHS, saving public money and improving the health of the country's heaviest drinkers, this could be a significant and positive step towards a healthier nation.

When you make the decision to do something unproductive like browsing Reddit instead of doing work, your brain is likely engaging in a process called cognitive dissonance. This is when two conflicting thoughts or beliefs exist at the same time, resulting in mental discomfort and tension. Your brain is weighing the pros and cons of each activity and deciding which one will provide more pleasure or reward in the moment (in this case, browsing Reddit). In order to relieve the tension, it pushes away the thought of doing work and focuses on the activity that provides more reward, even if it isn't the most productive option.

This discovery has opened up a debate about whether Apple is unfairly promoting its own apps in the App Store at the expense of rival developers. Apple has denied any wrongdoing, stating that its apps are held to the same rigorous review process as those of third-party developers. Sensor Tower's study analyzed the top 50 search terms in the App Store during the first half of 2019. The study found that Apple's own apps ranked first in 60 of the search terms analyzed. For example, when users searched for terms such as "music," "maps," and "video," Apple's own apps topped the search results. One possible explanation for this could be that Apple's own apps are simply the most popular in their respective categories. After all, Apple's Music app has been around since 2015 and has steadily evolved into a comprehensive streaming service. Similarly, Apple Maps has improved significantly since its initial release in 2012 and has become a reliable navigation tool for many users. However, some developers argue that Apple's position as the owner of the App Store gives its apps an unfair advantage. They claim that Apple has been using its power to prioritize its own apps in search results over its rivals' apps, which can negatively impact smaller developers who are struggling to get their apps noticed. This is not the first time that Apple has faced criticism over its App Store practices. In 2019, the company was accused of artificially inflating App Store search ads for its own apps. Apple was also embroiled in an antitrust investigation in Europe, which alleged that the company was favoring its own apps over rivals' apps. Apple has always maintained that it is committed to providing a level playing field in the App Store for all developers. The company claims that its priority is to deliver the best possible experience for users by promoting apps that are high-quality, safe, and meet the App Store's strict guidelines. The App Store is a vital component of the iOS ecosystem, and it's no surprise that Apple wants to ensure that its own apps are showcased prominently. However, the recent study by Sensor Tower has raised concerns about whether Apple's policies are fair to third-party developers. As the app market continues to evolve, it's crucial that Apple remains transparent about its practices and fosters an environment that is fair to all developers, big and small. The Soviet Invasion of Afghanistan In April of 1978, the Marxist People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan seized power in a coup d'etat, killing the previous leader, Mohammad Daoud Khan. The new regime implemented a series of reforms aimed at modernizing the country and establishing a socialist state, such as equal rights for women and land reform. However, these reforms alienated traditional Afghan tribes, and many members of the country's Muslim majority, who saw them as a threat to their way of life. In July of 1979, the Afghan government was overthrown by another coup d'etat, this time led by Hafizullah Amin. However, Amin was opposed by the Soviet Union, which viewed him as an unreliable ally, and his attempts to improve relations with the West. In December of 1979, Soviet troops invaded Afghanistan and toppled the Amin regime. Amin was killed, and replaced by Babrak Karmal, a pro-Soviet leader. The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan was initially supported by the United States, which saw it as an opportunity to contain the spread of communism. However, the invasion quickly turned into a quagmire, as the Soviets faced stiff resistance from Afghan rebel groups known as the Mujahideen. The Soviet Union withdrew from Afghanistan in 1989, and the Afghan Communist regime collapsed in 1992. The Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan would lead to the rise of the Taliban, an Islamic fundamentalist group, which would rule Afghanistan from 1996 until 2001. Iran-Contra Affair The Iran-Contra Affair was a scandal that erupted during the administration of US President Ronald Reagan. In the early 1980s, the Reagan administration began secretly selling arms to Iran in an attempt to secure the release of American hostages being held in Lebanon by Iranian-backed terrorist groups. However, the sale of arms to Iran violated an American arms embargo, and the proceeds from the sales were used to fund the Contra rebels in Nicaragua, who were fighting against the socialist Sandinista government. The affair came to light in November of 1986, when a plane carrying American arms to Iran crashed in the jungle in Nicaragua. Reagan denied any knowledge of the arms sales, but investigations by Congress revealed that several members of his administration, including National Security Adviser John Poindexter and Assistant Secretary of State Elliott Abrams, had been involved in the scheme. Reagan was not impeached, but the scandal severely damaged his reputation, and led to the resignation of several members of his administration.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Lily who always seemed to be followed by her shadow. She never really thought much of it until one day when she noticed that her shadow was moving independently of her. At first, Lily simply found it odd and amusing, but as time went on, her shadow began to take on a sinister quality. Every time she turned around, her shadow seemed to be growing larger and more menacing, as if it was trying to swallow her up. Lily began to feel as though her shadow was turning against her. She tried to ignore it, hoping that it would simply go away on its own, but it only seemed to be getting worse. Eventually, she realized that she needed to do something to stop her shadow before it consumed her completely. She spent weeks researching and trying different methods, but nothing seemed to work. It seemed as though her shadow was determined to destroy her, no matter what she did. Finally, Lily had an idea - what if she could lure her shadow into a trap and weaken it? She spent hours constructing a complex system of mirrors and lenses that could focus light into a single beam, and then she waited until the sun was at just the right angle. She stood in front of the apparatus, waiting for her shadow to come within range. Finally, it did. Her shadow stretched out, looming over her menacingly as it always did. But this time, Lily was ready. She activated the device, and a powerful beam of light shot out, striking her shadow directly. For a moment, nothing seemed to happen, but then Lily heard a strange gnashing noise, and her shadow began to shrink and struggle. Finally, it faded away entirely, leaving Lily alone and victorious. From that day forward, Lily was more careful about her shadows. She still felt as though they were watching her at times, but she knew that she had the power to protect herself against them if they ever turned against her again.

In a significant development for the world energy market, the price of oil has fallen to its lowest level since 2009. This drop comes as global production continues to remain high, setting the stage for a prolonged period of lower energy costs for consumers and businesses around the world. The price of a barrel of Brent crude fell to 36.16, its lowest point since July 2004, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slumped to 33.59 per barrel, also the lowest since 2009. The drop in oil prices is a result of a global oversupply of crude oil caused by increased production from the United States, Middle East, and Russia. The rise in production has been driven by technology advancements and higher investment in oil exploration in recent years. With oil producers continuing to focus on maintaining their market share, the oversupply is expected to persist well into 2021. This is good news for consumers, as it means lower prices for gasoline, diesel fuel, and heating oil. The global energy watchdog, the International Energy Agency (IEA), recently revised its forecasts for global oil demand as a result of the pandemic. The IEA expects global oil demand to drop by 8.1 million barrels per day in 2020, more than the 7.9 million barrels per day it predicted last month. The impact of the drop in oil prices will be felt across various sectors of the economy, with transportation, manufacturing, and construction among the industries likely to benefit the most from lower energy costs. While the lower prices are a relief for consumers, the financial implications of the decline in oil prices are significant for oil-producing countries. The countries that rely heavily on oil exports will face reduced government revenue, which could impact public services deployment since oil revenue is usually a significant source of their revenue. It remains to be seen how long the dip in oil prices will last, but experts predict that the oversupply will continue for the foreseeable future. In the meantime, consumers are set to enjoy lower energy costs at the pump and at home.

The dungeon was dark and damp, filled with the stench of fear that seemed to cling to its walls. The torturer had been in this room for many years, performing his craft on those unfortunate souls who did not follow the laws of the kingdom. But today, he was about to try something new. He had heard tales of an unlikely form of torture being used by some of the more creative criminals: laughter. He had always been intrigued by this idea, so he decided to give it a try in his own dungeon room. The torturer began by making jokes and telling stories, trying to get his victims to laugh. At first, they refused, too scared to let out any sound. But as the torturer kept going, some began to find humor in his words and eventually, a few brave souls laughed. The torturer was pleased with his success, and he continued to make jokes, getting louder and more outrageous each time. Soon, all of his victims were in fits of laughter, unable to stop no matter how hard they tried. The laughter filled the dungeon, echoing off the walls and reverberating through the air. It was a strange sight to see, but the torturer knew he had achieved his goal. He had broken his victims down, using laughter instead of violence, and he was satisfied with his work. From then on, the torturer used laughter as his primary method of torture. Although it was an unlikely choice, it proved to be incredibly effective.

Ever since she was a child, Samantha had always felt like she was different from everyone else. She couldn't quite put her finger on it, but she had a sneaking suspicion that she had some kind of special power. As she grew older, this feeling only intensified. Now in her early twenties, she was almost certain that she had superpowers. Of course, she couldn't be completely sure. Superpowers weren't exactly a common occurrence, after all. But Samantha had read all the stories, watched all the movies. She knew that there were people out there who could fly, or shoot fire from their hands, or become invisible at will. And she just had this sense that she was one of them. Samantha had spent countless hours testing her powers, trying to figure out exactly what she could do. She had tried to move objects with her mind, to summon lightning from the sky, to teleport across the room. So far, nothing had worked. But she was convinced that there was something there, just out of reach. The problem was, if she was 100 sure that she had superpowers, her life would be completely different. She would have to come out of hiding, to show the world what she was capable of. And that was terrifying. Samantha had read enough comics to know that people with powers often ended up as targets, either for the government or for villains. She didn't want that kind of attention. But every day, the sense that she was meant for something more grew stronger. And she couldn't shake the feeling that the only way to truly know was to take the leap of faith, to put herself out there and see what happened. Samantha knew that this could either be the greatest decision of her life, or the biggest mistake she ever made. But for better or for worse, she was ready to find out once and for all if she had superpowers.

Junior doctors in England are to be balloted on industrial action over government plans to introduce a new contract from August 2016. The British Medical Association (BMA) has announced the ballot of its members nationwide, following an ongoing dispute with the Department of Health over proposed changes to the junior doctors' contract. The BMA has said that it is "dismayed" by the Government's refusal to negotiate on the terms of the new contract, and believes the proposed changes will have a detrimental effect on patient care and safety. If a majority of junior doctors vote in favour of industrial action, it could disrupt NHS services across England. This follows a series of strikes by junior doctors earlier this year, which saw hundreds of thousands of appointments and operations cancelled or postponed. Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt said the Government was "disappointed" that the BMA had chosen to pursue industrial action, claiming that the proposed contract offered a "fair deal" for both junior doctors and taxpayers. He also defended the Government's handling of the dispute, stating that the terms of the new contract would lead to safer working hours and improved career progression for junior doctors. However, Dr Johann Malawana, chair of the BMA's junior doctor committee, said he did not believe the current proposals were fair or reasonable, and accused the Government of making junior doctors "the scapegoats for wider problems in the NHS." The BMA has said that it intends to work closely with NHS Employers to ensure that any action taken by junior doctors is carefully considered and minimises disruption for patients. It is also encouraging members to take part in the upcoming ballot, in order to have their voices heard. The results of the ballot will be announced in early June, and industrial action could begin as soon as August.

I had driven past the decrepit, shitty building at least a thousand times since moving into the apartment complex it sat next to, constantly polluting the space in which I lived. I had always assumed it was abandoned, as the windows were boarded up and there was no sign of life inside. But one day, I noticed a small flicker of light coming from inside. Curiosity getting the better of me, I parked my car and approached the building. As I got closer, I could see that there was indeed someone inside, moving around with a flashlight. Fighting the urge to turn away and forget about what I had seen, I knocked on the door. After a few moments of silence, the door creaked open, revealing a man in his 50s with a wild beard and unkempt hair. "What do you want?" he growled. "I just wanted to make sure everything was okay," I replied, trying to sound as friendly as possible. "I've never seen anyone in here before." The man eyed me suspiciously for a moment, then shrugged. "I'm just fixing some stuff up," he said gruffly. "Nothing to worry about." I nodded, feeling relieved but still uneasy. "Well, if you need any help or anything, just let me know. I live right over there," I gestured towards my apartment complex. As I turned to leave, the man called after me. "Hey, kid... thanks." I smiled and waved, feeling like I had made a small difference in someone's day. From then on, I often left a friendly note or a plate of food by the building, just to let the man know that someone cared.

The thread sparked a conversation about how to find a job that aligns with these preferences. Additionally, they recommended seeking out companies that primarily operate from their physical location. Other commenters suggested expanding one's search beyond a specific geographical location and looking into more niche industries that might not be as likely to rely on remote work. Considering smaller, regional companies in specific industries could enhance one's likelihood of finding an in-office job. Once upon a time, there were two cities that existed on two different sides of a vast ocean. One city only had men, while the other only had women living in it. The cities were separated by the ocean and the inhabitants of both cities were forbidden to cross it except for one day every year. Each year, on the day of the summer solstice, the male and female inhabitants of the two cities would build two huge rafts and, at the stroke of midnight, they would float them out onto the ocean through the city's ports. It was said that the rafts were made from the strongest wood, and that the men and women worked tirelessly to build them, in preparation for the annual meeting to come. As the rafts approached each other, the anticipation and excitement in both cities was palpable. Everyone knew that this was the only time they could meet, so the excitement was understandable. The men and women would sit across from each other, and they would spend the night singing, dancing, and sharing stories. They would talk about their daily lives, their hopes, their dreams, and their aspirations. They would share meals and break bread together, and they would open their hearts to each other. As the night wore on, the sun began to rise and the two rafts would begin their journey back to their respective cities. The men and women would wave goodbye to each other, and they would promise to see each other next year. Despite the distance and the separation that existed between them, the men and women of the two cities knew that they had a special bond. They knew that their shared experience of a night spent together had created a sense of unity between them, a sense of appreciation for each other's differences, and a desire to strengthen the bond that existed between them. For the inhabitants of the two cities, the yearly meeting was a magical and special event, one that they all looked forward to with great anticipation. It was an event that reminded them of the beauty of human connection, and the importance of cherishing the things that bring us together, even if they are only fleeting moments.

He took an old bucket and filled it with snow from the mountain top. Then he placed the ice cream inside the bucket and hoped that the coldness of the snow would keep the ice cream cool. The experiment seemed to work at first. But as the sun beat down on the bucket, the snow began to melt, letting in more heat and quickly melting the ice cream. The villagers had no choice but to think of something else. One of them suggested using blocks of ice from the nearby lake, which seemed to work much better than the snow had. The villagers were relieved to find a solution to their ice cream conundrum. From then on, they used blocks of ice from the lake to keep their ice cream cool all summer long.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emily who had always wanted a pet. One day, Emily's parents surprised her with two options: a bird or a hamster. Emily was thrilled! She had no idea which one to choose, but she was determined to make the right decision. The hamster was cute and cuddly, but it didn't have the same level of interaction and needed a lot of exercise. After much thought and consideration, Emily ultimately decided on the hamster. She loved the idea of having a little furry friend to play with and take care of. Despite the bird's charm, it just didn't seem like the right fit for her. Emily named her hamster Benny and they quickly became inseparable. She spent hours playing with him and taking care of him every day. Though she never regretted her decision, Emily found herself wondering what it would have been like to have a bird instead. One day, her neighbor introduced Emily to his pet bird named Charlie. Emily was fascinated and amazed by how smart and colorful he was. She couldn't help but feel a little bit jealous of her neighbor for having such a wonderful pet. However, over time, Emily realized that Benny was the perfect pet for her after all. They had developed a very special bond and she wouldn't trade him for anything in the world. She had made the right decision in choosing a hamster, and she was proud to call Benny her little buddy.

Outrun lets you execute local commands using the processing power of another Linux machine. The commands don't need to be installed on the other machine, and local files and paths are resolved automatically. Usage: outrun command [arguments...] The command is executed on the remote machine and the output displayed locally in your terminal. If you don't pass an explicit command, a new shell session is started on the remote machine. You can then enter commands as normal. This can be useful for transferring files or inspecting a remote system. Setup First, create a local configuration file at .outrunrc . It should look something like this: [server] host "localhost" username "bob" port 22 Then install the server component on the machine you want to use for processing: sudo pip3 install outrun-server or, for MacOS: brew tap bobbytablestap brew install outrun-server Note that the server component requires Python 3.6. How it works Outrun uses SSH to transfer files and execute commands. By default, On macOS and Linux, key authentication is used and no password prompt should appear. On Windows, the command prompt is used to enter the password instead of using key authentication. When you run a command, the command is first built into an executable binary with PyInstaller. This binary is then transferred to the server and executed. Local files, like data files and libraries, are bundled up and transferred along with the binary. Documentation Full documentation is available at , including installation instructions for Windows and MacOS. Development To work on Outrun locally, clone this repository and create a virtual environment with python -m venv .env . Then activate the environment with source .envbinactivate and install all requirements with pip install -r requirements.txt . Running tests Outrun's tests depend on Docker Compose and make sure to have it installed and running before running the tests. The tests are organized into three levels: Unit tests: These tests can be run with make test . They test Outrun's internals, and don't require any network connection. Integration tests: These tests can be run with make test-integration . They exercise the entire Outrun toolchain from end-to-end (client, server and PyInstaller) and don't require any network connection. E2E tests: These tests can be run with make test-e2e . They test the entire Outrun toolchain from end-to-end, but do so against a real SSH server. The tests will run on the localhost if you have an SSH server configured, otherwise they'll run against a temporary Docker container. Releasing Before releasing a new version, update the CHANGELOG with changes since the previous release. To create a new release, run make release VERSIONx.y.z , where x.y.z is the new version number. This will update version in outruninit.py , tag the current commit with the new version and push to GitHub. Once the release has been tagged, Travis will build the binaries and push them to PyPI.

Video moment retrieval is to search the moment that is most relevant to the given natural language query. Existing methods are mostly trained in a fully-supervised setting, which requires the training dataset to be manually annotated with both the video moment and its corresponding query. This makes the data collection process expensive and time-consuming. To address this issue, we propose a weakly supervised approach for video moment retrieval. Our method only requires the video moment annotation during the training stage, without any manual query annotation. We use an external language model to generate various natural language queries for each video moment, and then use these automatically generated queries as pseudo-labels during training. Experimental results show that our proposed approach is able to achieve comparable performance to the fully-supervised setting on the ActivityNet Captions dataset.

The fuzzy K -means problem is a generalization of the classical K -means problem to soft clusterings, i.e. clusterings where each points belongs to each cluster to some degree. Although the classical K-means problem assigns each point to a single cluster, the fuzzy K-means problem assigns each point to all clusters with degrees of membership representing how likely the point belongs to each cluster. The fuzzy K-means problem is also known as FCM (fuzzy c-means) and is commonly used in pattern recognition and image segmentation. In fuzzy K-means, the objective is to minimize the sum of squared distances between each point and its cluster center, weighted by the degree of membership. The degree of membership of each point to each cluster is computed using a membership function which gives a value between 0 and 1, representing the probability or degree of belief that the point belongs to that cluster. The membership function is updated iteratively until convergence is reached. Fuzzy K-means has several advantages over classical K-means, including the ability to handle overlapping clusters and the ability to assign points to multiple clusters simultaneously. It also allows for more nuanced representations of cluster membership and a finer-grained analysis of data. However, fuzzy K-means can be computationally intensive and requires careful tuning of parameters.
