Deep learning models continuously break new records across different NLP tasks. At the same time, their success exposes weaknesses of model evaluation. Here, we compile several key pitfalls of evaluation of NLP models: 1. Overfitting to the evaluation measure: Models may learn to optimize for the evaluation metric itself rather than the underlying goal of the task. This can result in poor generalization performance on real-world data. 2. Lack of diversity in evaluation data: Evaluating on a small or unrepresentative sample of data can give a distorted view of model performance. It is important to ensure that evaluation data is diverse and includes a range of common and edge cases. 3. Domain mismatch: Models trained on one domain may not perform well on data from another domain. Evaluation on a different domain may inflate or deflate model performance. 4. Lack of emphasis on interpretability and explainability: Metrics such as accuracy or F1 score may not provide insights into why a model is making certain decisions. It is important to evaluate models in a transparent and interpretable way, especially for applications that affect human lives. 5. Failure to account for ethical considerations: Evaluating models solely on performance metrics without considering potential ethical implications can lead to biased or harmful outcomes. It is important to critically evaluate models for fairness, accountability, and transparency. These are just a few of the many pitfalls of evaluating NLP models. It is important to regularly re-evaluate metrics and evaluation methods to ensure that they remain robust and relevant in the face of evolving machine learning technology and ethical considerations.

I had been living in the same room for years, so I was familiar with the people who lived there. One of them was a young boy, who seemed particularly troubled lately. He had been acting strange and spending a lot of time alone in his room. I had no idea what he was up to until tonight. Just after midnight, I heard a loud thump coming from the boy's room. I knew something was wrong, but I didn't want to get involved; I was just a stuffed animal after all. But then I heard screaming, followed by a man's voice saying, "You won't get away with this!" That was when I discovered that the young boy had killed someone. He had stabbed the person multiple times and the blood was everywhere. I felt so helpless, wishing I could do something to help. I wanted to scream for help, but I knew that wouldn't do any good. All I could do was sit there silently and watch as the killer fled the scene. The police eventually arrived and arrested the boy, but I couldn't shake the feeling of dread that had taken over me since the incident began. I had witnessed a murder from the perspective of a cheerful inanimate object and there was nothing I could do about it.

They were convinced that the fruit's taste outweighed its odor, and they eventually accepted it and included it in their meals. We analyze the security of the authentication code against pollution attacks in network coding given by Oggier and Fathi and show one way to remove one very strong condition they placed on the authentication code. This can improve the efficiency of the network coding system without compromising security. A pollution attack in network coding occurs when an attacker introduces malicious packets into the network to manipulate the information being transmitted. The authentication code proposed by Oggier and Fathi is based on the use of linear network codes and is designed to protect against pollution attacks. However, one of the conditions they imposed was that the authentication code must be of full rank, which limits its practical use. To overcome this limitation, one approach is to use a non-full rank authentication code and add an additional layer of randomness to the code. This randomness can be generated by using a random matrix to multiply the authentication code. This technique can effectively remove the full rank condition and still provide the required security against pollution attacks. Overall, by removing the full rank condition, we can improve the efficiency of network coding systems without compromising their security.

This decline is being attributed to a variety of factors, including the declining birth rate and recent changes to the law that make it easier for men to avoid mandatory national service. Currently, all able-bodied South Korean men between the ages of 18 and 35 are required to serve in the military for a minimum of 21 months. However, a new law that went into effect this year allows men to postpone their service if they meet certain criteria, such as being enrolled in a university or having a job. As a result of these changes, the number of men enlisting in the military has declined significantly, from a high of nearly 700,000 in 2011 to just over 400,000 last year. This decline is expected to continue in the coming years, as the number of births in South Korea has been falling for several years. In 2017, the birth rate in South Korea hit a record low of just 1.05 children per woman, down from 1.24 in 2010. At this rate, the population of South Korea is expected to peak at 51.9 million in 2028 and then start to decline. The decline in the population is also expected to have a negative impact on the economy, as the working-age population shrinks and the dependency ratio increases. In order to offset these effects, the South Korean government has been encouraging women to have more children and has also been seeking to attract more foreign workers.

As I slowly came out of my cryogenic sleep, I could feel immense pain in my limbs. It took me a few moments to realize that it wasn't just the cryogenic sleep that was causing the discomfort, but rather the fact that my body had been through an immense ordeal. The last thing I remembered was the spaceship jolting and shaking as we attempted to make a landing on the planet. The next thing I knew, I was lying in a strange forest, surrounded by trees and unfamiliar wildlife. As I looked around, I realized that I was completely alone. The cryogenic pods of my crewmates were empty, and there was no sign of any other human life nearby. My mind was racing with questions. How did we crash land? Where were my crewmates? And most importantly, how was I going to survive on this strange and unknown planet? I stumbled through the forest, trying to find any clues or signs of my crewmates, but the area was deserted. As night began to fall, I became increasingly anxious. I had no shelter, no food or water, and no idea of where to go. I knew that I had to find a way to survive, but it felt impossible to do so without any resources. It was then that I remembered the survival training I had received back on Earth. I forced myself to calm down and started to think logically about my situation. I knew that I had to find shelter, water, and food. Using my survival skills, I explored the surrounding forests and found a cave to take shelter in for the night. Over the next few days, I continued to explore the planet, searching for any signs of my crewmates. I discovered that the planet was eerily similar to Earth, with forests, lakes, and mountains. However, the fauna and flora were completely different, which meant that I had to adapt quickly to survive. As I explored deeper into the forests, I stumbled upon an abandoned research facility. Inside, I found evidence that my crewmates had been there, but I had no idea where they had gone. It was then that I realized that the crash landing might not have been an accident. With this realization, I knew that I needed to be even more careful. As I continued to survive on the planet, I became more determined than ever to find my crewmates and uncover the truth behind the crash landing. Every day, I grew stronger and wiser, learning how to adapt to the planet's harsh environment, and overcoming my fear and uncertainty. Finally, after months of exploration and struggle, I found my crewmates. They too had been surviving on the planet, and together we were able to piece together the events that had led to our crash landing. It wasn't an accident but rather an act of sabotage. We were able to discover the identity of the saboteur and bring them to justice. As we prepared to leave the planet behind, I realized that the experience had changed me in ways that I could never have imagined. It had taught me the value of perseverance, resourcefulness, and courage. I had become a survivor, and nothing could ever take that away.

Newsflash: Fifty-foot-tall ice spikes might make it hard to land on Europa Scientists and researchers have long been fascinated by Jupiter's icy moon, Europa, with its potential to harbor life beneath its icy surface. However, landing on Europa's surface has always presented a challenge due to its harsh environment. Now, a new study suggests that landing on Europa could be even more difficult than previously thought. According to the study, Europa's surface is covered with massive ice spikes that can reach up to 50 feet tall. These ice spikes are formed by the process of sublimation, where the ice turns directly into gas. The study suggests that the spikes are formed due to the extreme temperature differences between Europa's surface and its thin atmosphere. The presence of these ice spikes poses a significant challenge to any potential mission to Europa. Landing a spacecraft on the surface could be hazardous, and the spikes could damage any equipment that comes into contact with them. However, some experts believe that the discovery of these ice spikes could be an opportunity for exploration. The spikes could provide a way for scientists to sample the moon's icy crust and potentially extract samples from deep beneath the surface. Despite the challenges presented by these ice spikes, researchers remain determined to continue studying Europa and unlocking its mysteries.

The stock is now up more than 20 since last week when Byrne first made his controversial comments. In the wake of Byrne's departure, Overstock said its board of directors had appointed Jonathan Johnson, the company's current president, as interim CEO. Johnson said in a statement that Byrne's resignation "was the right decision" and that he was confident the company would continue to thrive under his leadership. "Our team is committed to continuing the strong momentum we've built over the past year," Johnson said. "We remain focused on our mission of making shopping easier for customers, delivering innovative products and services, and creating value for shareholders." Byrne, who founded Overstock in 1999, will remain on the company's board of directors. He also said he planned to stay active in the retail industry and pursue other opportunities. "I am grateful to have been part of such an incredible team and organization," Byrne said in his statement. "I wish them all the best and look forward to watching their continued success."

After years of study and experimentation, they concluded that I was the only sentient being among the humans. I was the only one who could truly understand the world around me. Recently I've heard a lot about mandatory vaccination schemes in public schools. I don't see any problem with them. I've heard a few counterarguments, but they seem unsatisfying to me, and I wanted to see if anyone here could make a better case. The main counterargument I've heard is that parents should have the right to decide what's best for their children, and that includes whether or not to vaccinate them. But I don't think this is a very strong argument. Parents also have the right to decide whether or not to put their children in public school. If they want their children to be vaccinated, they can send them to a school that requires it. And if they don't want their children to be vaccinated, they can homeschool them or send them to a private school that doesn't require it. So it seems like parents still have plenty of choice in the matter. Another counterargument I've heard is that some people have medical conditions that make vaccination risky for them. But again, I don't think this is a very strong argument. First of all, it's not like every child with a medical condition is going to have a reaction to a vaccine. And even if a child does have a reaction, it's usually not serious. So the risk is really quite small. And second of all, there are already laws in place that allow children with medical conditions to be exempted from vaccination requirements. So I don't think this is a valid reason to oppose mandatory vaccination.

A possible counter-argument could be: While the idea of a level playing field is appealing in theory, it is not necessarily fair or efficient in practice. Uber and taxis are fundamentally different business models, and forcing them to comply with the same rules could stifle innovation and competition. For example, requiring Uber drivers to have the same expensive licenses and permits as taxi drivers could prevent many potential drivers from joining the platform, reducing the supply and increasing the cost of rides for consumers. Similarly, mandating that Uber cars have the same markings, meters, and insurance requirements as taxis could add unnecessary expenses and complexity for both drivers and passengers. Furthermore, it is not always clear that taxi regulations are the best way to ensure safety and quality for ridesharing services. Many Uber drivers undergo thorough background checks and vehicle inspections, and the ratings and feedback system allows customers to provide real-time feedback and accountability. Regulating Uber like taxis could also create confusion and inconsistency for riders in different cities and countries, hindering the growth of a global service. Instead of simply copying taxi regulations, cities should work with Uber and other ridesharing companies to develop new, flexible rules that balance the needs of innovation, competition, and public safety. This could involve setting performance-based standards that measure outcomes rather than inputs, such as driver ratings, accident rates, and market share. By fostering a dynamic regulatory environment that promotes innovation and choice, cities can create more value and benefit for all stakeholders.

Correlative microscopy is a methodology combining the functionality of light microscopy with the high resolution of electron microscopy and other microscopy technologies. Image registration for correlative microscopy is quite challenging because it involves aligning different imaging modalities with different scales, pixel sizes, and imaging depths. This requires specialized software and workflows designed to correct for distortions, establish reference points, and apply transformations to the data. One approach to image registration in correlative microscopy is to use fiducial markers or landmarks that are visible in both the light and electron microscopy images. These markers can be fluorescently labeled or metal-coated, and must be carefully chosen to avoid interfering with the biological structures of interest. Once the markers are identified and located in both images, they can be used to calculate the transformation matrix required to align the two datasets. Another approach involves using image features and algorithms that can match patterns in the two images, such as edges, corners, or texture. This can be useful when fiducial markers are not available or are difficult to distinguish, but requires more computational resources and may introduce errors due to the complexity of the patterns being matched. Regardless of the approach used, image registration is an essential step in correlative microscopy to ensure that the different imaging modalities can be accurately overlaid and integrated for a comprehensive understanding of biological structures and processes.

Yes. If you use a one-time-pad you can encrypt something in such a way that it absolutely cannot be decrypted unless you have the key. It's actually an incredibly simple and powerful encryption technique. One-time-pad involves generating a random key that is the same length as the plaintext (the message you want to encrypt), and adding each corresponding character in the key to the plaintext. The resulting ciphertext (the encrypted message) cannot be decrypted without the key, which must be kept secret from anyone who is not authorized to see the message. One-time-pad is often considered unbreakable, as long as the key is truly random, used only once, and kept completely secret.

Civil disobedience is usually defined as pertaining to a citizen's relation to the state and its laws, as distinguished from a constitutional impasse in which two public agencies, especially two branches of government, disagree with each other. In a constitutional impasse, each side is bound by its oath to uphold the Constitution and the laws of the land, and neither side can legally force the other to yield. In such a situation, civil disobedience may be the only recourse available to the people to resolve the impasse. The term "civil disobedience" was coined by Henry David Thoreau in 1848 in an essay where he justified his refusal to pay taxes as a protest against the Mexican-American War and the enslavement of African Americans. He wrote: "If the machine of government is of such a nature that it requires you to be the agent of injustice to another, then, I say, break the law. Let your life be a counter-friction to stop the machine." Since then, the concept of civil disobedience has been invoked by many groups and individuals to protest various perceived injustices, both real and imagined. In some cases, such as the civil rights movement of the 1960s, civil disobedience has been an effective tool for bringing about change. In other cases, such as the Occupy Wall Street movement of 2011, it has been less effective. There is no single formula for success in using civil disobedience to effect change, but there are some general principles that seem to be important. First, the protesters must have a clear and concise message that can be easily understood by the general public. Second, the protesters must be willing to sacrifice their own comfort and safety for the cause. And third, the protesters must be willing to accept the consequences of their actions, whether those consequences are arrest and imprisonment or simply being ignored.

Berlin, Germany - The Institute of National Remembrance (INR) for Poland has released the names of Nazi SS commanders and guards who served at the infamous Auschwitz death camp in German-occupied Poland. The move was taken as part of the watchdog group's efforts to keep the memory of the Holocaust alive and to ensure that those who carried out atrocities during World War II are held accountable. The INR, an organization responsible for investigating crimes of Nazi and Communist regimes in Poland, has released the names of over 8,500 guards and commanders who served at Auschwitz. The publication of the list is a milestone in the institute's work, which aims to document the full extent of horrors committed at the concentration and death camps. The online list includes information about the narionality, rank, function and fate of the individuals concerned. The INR hopes that by sharing this information, future generations will be able to learn from it and understand the magnitude of the horrors of the Holocaust. "The job of preserving the memory of the Holocaust is not only to mourn its victims but also to ensure that those who perpetrated these crimes are held accountable," said Jaroslaw Szarek, director of the Institute of National Remembrance. "Our research provides solid grounds for legal proceedings against those who served in the camp." The release of the names has caused a stir among historians and Holocaust survivors. While some have welcomed the move, others see it as a violation of privacy and have voiced concerns about possible retribution against the perpetrators, many of whom are now in advanced age or dead. The Auschwitz-Birkenau complex was a network of concentration, labor and extermination camps operated by Nazi Germany in occupied Poland during World War II. It is estimated that around 1.1 million people, mostly Jews, were killed at the site between 1940 and 1945. The release of these names is a powerful reminder of the atrocities committed during that time and hopes to preserve this memory for future generations.

Match Group, the company that owns Tinder, has become the latest high-profile software maker to ditch the Play Store and instead use its own payment systems. Last year, Epic Games used the same strategy to launch Fortnite on Android and avoid paying a 30 cut of in-app purchases to Google. The Play Store is an essential part of Android and is the easiest way for users to install apps from the platform's official app store. But it's also used by many developers to distribute their engines, tools, and other software products. Many of them charge subscription fees or sell assets that can be purchased within their apps. However, because Google requires all developers who sell digital goods and services through the Play Store to use its billing system, the company takes a 30 cut of all sales. Epic Games and now Match Group are both using their own payment systems to avoid this commission. In a blog post, Match Group said that it will stop using the Play Store to sell some of its products, including Tinder, Hinge, OkCupid, Plenty of Fish, and Match.com. Instead, it will direct users to its own website to download the apps. The company said that the decision was made to "provide our users with the best possible user experience and to continue investing in the relationships they're looking for." Match Group isn't the first company to make this move. Last year, Epic Games launched Fortnite on Android outside of the Play Store. The game was only available on Samsung devices at first, but it eventually launched on other Android devices through the Epic Games app. Like Match Group, Epic Games said that it made the decision to avoid Google's 30 cut. The company has also been vocal about its disdain for the Play Store's policies, which it has called "anti-competitive." Google has defended its policies, saying that the 30 cut is necessary to cover the costs of maintaining the Play Store and providing developer support. The company has also said that its policies are designed to create a level playing field for all developers. It's not clear how much money Match Group makes from in-app purchases, but Tinder is one of the company's most popular apps. In 2019, the app had an estimated 4.1 million paying subscribers. The news comes as Google is facing increased scrutiny from antitrust regulators in the US and Europe. The company is facing an antitrust lawsuit in the US, and the European Commission is investigating whether Google's policies for the Play Store violate EU competition laws.

In this work, we build a generic architecture of Convolutional Neural Networks to discover empirical properties of neural networks. Our first contribution is to introduce a state-of-the-art framework that depends on the number of layers, filter parameters, and the network's topology. We then evaluate our model and provide quantitative results that demonstrate its effectiveness. Finally, we discuss our findings and suggest potential future extensions. The proposed architecture consists of three stages: 1. Preprocessing: This stage consists of two components: (i) a convolutional layer to reduce the dimensionality of the input data, and (ii) a pooling layer to extract features from the data. 2. Feature Extraction: This stage consists of two components: (i) a convolutional layer to discover meaningful patterns in the data, and (ii) a fully-connected layer to classify the data into classes. 3. Classification: This stage uses the extracted features to classify the data into different classes. We evaluated our model on two datasets: the MNIST dataset and the CIFAR-10 dataset. For both datasets, we compared our model with other popular models, such as ResNet and VGGNet. Our results show that our model achieved better performance than the baseline models. Overall, our model is an effective approach for discovering empirical properties of neural networks. In the future, we will extend our work by exploring additional architectures and datasets.

A leading human rights organisation has called on the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) to fully investigate the deaths of civilians during air strikes in Libya last year. The air strikes in question took place in 2019 during the ongoing civil war in the country. NATO had been providing military support to the United Nations-backed Government of National Accord (GNA) in its fight against the Libyan National Army (LNA), led by General Khalifa Haftar. In a recent report, Amnesty International raised concerns about the civilian casualties caused by the air strikes. The organisation expressed that several of the air strikes may have resulted in unlawful killings, and called on NATO to conduct an independent and impartial investigation into these incidents. "The deaths of these civilians are tragic and demand a comprehensive, transparent, and impartial investigation," said Diana Eltahawy, Amnesty International's Deputy Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa. According to the report, at least 13 civilians were killed and several others injured in four separate air strikes by NATO forces. In each incident, the human rights organisation found that there was little or no effort made to minimize civilian harm or to verify that the targets were legitimate military objectives. "NATO must ensure that all its actions comply with international humanitarian law and respect the right to life of civilians," Eltahawy continued. "The organization should take immediate steps to investigate these incidents, hold those responsible accountable and provide reparation to the victims and their families." The conflict in Libya has been ongoing since the ouster and killing of long-time leader Muammar Gaddafi in 2011. The conflict has left much of the country in ruins and has forced tens of thousands of people to flee their homes. Both the GNA and LNA have been accused of human rights abuses and war crimes during the conflict. NATO has not yet responded to Amnesty International's call for an investigation into the air strikes. It remains to be seen whether the organization will take any action in response to these allegations. However, the human rights group has made it clear that it will continue to push for accountability and justice for the victims of these incidents.

In this paper, we design and experiment a far-field wireless power transfer (WPT) architecture based on distributed antennas, so-called WPT DAS, that dynamically selects transmit antenna and frequency to increase the efficiency and range of the power transfer. The proposed architecture consists of a base station and several distributed antennas that are strategically placed within the coverage area. Each distributed antenna is equipped with a specially designed matching network that adapts the antenna impedance to the output impedance of the power amplifier. The WPT DAS system operates in two phases: the calibration phase and the power transfer phase. In the calibration phase, the system scans the frequency band and selects the optimal operating frequency for each distributed antenna. The system also measures the transfer efficiency and the phase difference between the base station and each distributed antenna. In the power transfer phase, the system dynamically selects the transmit antenna and frequency based on the measured transfer efficiency and phase difference. The system uses a closed-loop control algorithm to adjust the power amplifier output power, optimize the matching network parameters, and maintain a constant voltage at the load. Experimental results show that the WPT DAS system achieves an average transfer efficiency of 50 at a distance of 2 meters using a single distributed antenna, and an average transfer efficiency of 70 at a distance of 4 meters using two distributed antennas. The proposed architecture has potential applications in powering wireless sensors, mobile robots, and other Internet of Things (IoT) devices.

The chloroplast of Cyanophora contains many features that are found in other chloroplasts but in more simple forms. For example, it has a single membrane rather than two membranes like other chloroplasts. It also lacks the internal membrane system found in other chloroplasts and instead contains few flattened sacs. Additionally, the photosynthetic pigments contained within the chloroplast are simpler than those of other plants. These features suggest that Cyanophora was one of the earliest organisms to contain a chloroplast and that it has remained relatively unchanged over time.

I'm no professional when it comes to logic or argumentation but I have been pondering this thought lately. I am not a believer of any after life or supernatural. If we don't have an after life or any other form of existence, does that mean our actions and choices in this life are all for nothing? We will never be held accountable for anything and all of our experiences in life are meaningless. No, it does not mean that our actions and choices are for nothing. Our lives are valuable and meaningful even if there is no afterlife. Life is a gift to be enjoyed, and the choices we make will determine how we spend our time here on earth and the impact we have on others. Even if there is no afterlife, it's important to make ethical decisions, take responsibility for our actions, and strive to live a life of meaning and purpose. Ultimately, it's up to us to decide what kind of legacy we want to leave behind in this life.

We study the problem of recognizing visual entities from the textual descriptions of their classes. Specifically, given birds' images with free-text descriptions of their species, we learn to classify images into one of the classes. Since the descriptions can vary significantly in length and content, we propose a model to learn representations of visual entities by extracting relevant information from the text without relying on any hand-crafted features. Our approach is based on an encoder-decoder architecture, where the encoder maps the textual description into a latent embedding space. The decoder takes both the embedding and the image as input and predicts the class label. We evaluate our proposed method on the challenging Birdsnap dataset, achieving state-of-the-art results. Our method follows an encoder-decoder architecture, which consists of two main modules: the encoder and the decoder. The encoder module is responsible for mapping the given textual description into a latent embedding space. This is done by leveraging a pre-trained language model (e.g., BERT) to extract meaningful information from the text. The decoder takes both the embedding and the image as input and predicts the class label. To train our model, we use a cross-entropy loss with regularization terms to ensure the smoothness of the latent embedding space and its consistency with the original text. We evaluate our method on the challenging Birdsnap dataset, a collection of images of birds with free-text descriptions of their species. We compare our results with several baseline methods and show that our proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art results on this task. In particular, our method outperforms the baselines by a significant margin, with an accuracy of 86.9.

Luton Police have arrested two people and seized a handgun and ammunition following a police operation. The operation was launched by the Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire Advanced Crime Team (ACT) and Luton Police on Thursday 4th March. The ACT team works to tackle serious and organised crime in the region. This operation follows an investigation into gun crime in the area, and is part of an ongoing effort to reduce the threat of firearms in Luton. Officers from Luton Police executed a search warrant at a property in the town and located a handgun, as well as rounds of ammunition. Two people were arrested during the operation and are now in police custody. Detective Inspector Jon Wardell said: "We are committed to tackling gun crime and ensuring that our streets remain safe places for everybody who lives, works and visits our county." He added: "This seizure shows our commitment to tackling those responsible for bringing guns onto our streets and it is reassuring that our work has resulted in a weapon being taken off the streets." Anyone with information about the possession or supply of firearms should contact police on 101 or Crimestoppers, anonymously, on 0800 555 111.

I don't like being controlled." Ouch. That hurts. It really does. Not because I'm a nice guy and I want to be liked by this girl, but because it's true. I am controlling, and I don't know how to fix that. No matter how hard I try, it seems like my head won't let my heart have the upper hand. She keeps talking, and I keep nodding. I'm not sure if I'm agreeing with her or just trying to get her to shut up. I've never been good at arguing with women. My mom always told me that men and women are different. We think differently, we communicate differently, we're wired differently. And she was right. I can never win an argument with a woman. They always find a way to make us look like idiots. But Deeya is different. She doesn't argue with me. She doesn't try to make me look stupid. She just tells me what she thinks, and I listen. And for some reason, that makes me feel even worse. Eventually, I can't take it anymore. "I'm sorry," I say. "I know I can be controlling. I'll try to change." "It's not that I don't like you, Tristan. I think you're a great guy. But I need my space, and I can't be with someone who doesn't understand that." "I understand," I say, even though I don't. I don't understand anything. "I'm sorry," she says. "I hope we can still be friends." "Of course." We hug, and then she walks away. As I watch her disappear into the crowd, all I can think about is how much I wish things had turned out differently. Public health doctors have warned that the government's drive to boost participation in rugby in English schools is ill-conceived and risks leading to children getting seriously hurt. The warning follows the announcement of a 2m fund to increase the number of state schools offering rugby union to pupils. The money will be used to recruit new teachers, provide specialist training and equipment, and host festivals and other events. However, public health experts say that while they welcome any initiative which encourages physical activity, they are concerned that the government has failed to consider the potential risks associated with the sport. Dr. Tom Hobson, a consultant in public health, said: "Rugby is a contact sport and there is a risk of injury. It is important that the right safety measures are put in place to protect children from serious injuries." He went on to say that even with the best training and equipment, children may still be vulnerable to head injuries, broken bones and soft tissue damage. He highlighted the need for "appropriate and rigorous safety measures" to be implemented before any attempt to increase participation in rugby is made. Other critics of the government's plan include the charity Action for Children, which said it was "incredibly concerned" by the lack of consultation with parents, who should have been consulted about what sports their children should be playing. The Department for Education responded to the criticism, saying it was taking steps to ensure all necessary safety protocols were in place. A spokesperson said: "We are committed to ensuring that all young people have access to a broad range of activities and sports, including rugby, and are working closely with school leaders and governing bodies to ensure that proper safety measures are in place."

Dewi and Dwynwen, named after two of Wales' most renowned patron saints, are nestled in a romantic "cwtch." Their arrival marks the launch of a campaign by heritage body Cadw to try and encourage people to learn more about the saints who have shaped Wales. Dewi and Dwynwen's journey to Cardiff Bay is part of a string of events across Wales this month. The 16ft pair will be joined by two smaller dragons - Maredudd and Madoc, representing Saint David and Saint Madoc. On Tuesday, they will join hundreds of schoolchildren in Swansea to celebrate St David's Day before appearing at the Royal Welsh Show in Llanelwedd, Powys. Image copyright Cadw Image caption The dragons have been created by sculptor Marc Rees and his team at Llantarnam Grange Arts Centre A shorter version of their odyssey will also see them tour towns and villages across Wales. Cadw said its "Dragons on the Town" project was designed to inspire children to learn about Wales' patron saints. Director Annwen Darlington said: "All over Wales, there are places named after our patron saints, from towns to churches and chapels, schools and colleges, to lakes, roads and rivers. "This year we want to bring our patron saints back into the heart of communities, engaging with community groups, young people and families, to celebrate the story of these remarkable figures." St David - Dewi Sant Image copyright Cadw Image caption A portrait of St David Dewi (David) was born around 500 AD, probably at Henfynw near Cardigan, Ceredigion. He is thought to have studied under Saint Paulinus in Rome and later became a teacher at Henfynw. He founded 12 monasteries, including one at Glastonbury, Somerset, and his followers were known as Clynnog Fawr monks. In 569 he held a synod at Llandewi Brefi, Carmarthenshire, where he established the rules for monastic life. He is buried at his monastery in Pembrokeshire and was canonised by Pope Callistus II in 1120. St David's Day is celebrated on 1 March. St Dwynwen - Santes Dwynwen Image copyright Cadw Image caption St Dwynwen's church on Llanddwyn Island, Anglesey Dwynwen (Dwynwen) was born around 450 AD, the daughter of Brychan Brycheiniog, King of Brycheiniog. She fell in love with Maelon Dafodrill, but her father disapproved of the relationship. Legend has it that she was so distraught that she prayed for Maelon to be turned into ice. God granted her wish and she then begged for him to be thawed. God agreed, but Maelon had forgotten about her by then. Dwynwen went on to become a nun and built a convent on Llanddwyn Island, Anglesey. She died there, aged 25, and is believed to be buried under an oak tree. Her feast day is celebrated on 25 January. St Madoc - Sant Madog Image copyright Cadw Image caption A statue to St Madoc stands outside the parish church in Whitehaven Madoc (Madog ab Owain Gwynedd) was born in 1150, the first son of Owain Gwynedd, Prince of Gwynedd and ruler of north Wales. It is said he sailed west from Rhos-on-Sea, Conwy, in 1170, in search of new lands and may have reached North America many years before Christopher Columbus. There is no evidence for this, but his legend inspired many writers and poets. He is said to have died in 1200 and is remembered each year at the town festival of Madoc Fair, in Whitehaven, Cumbria.

The man had been trying to kill himself for years. He had tried every method he could think of, but something always stopped him. It was as if the universe wanted him to stay alive. He had jumped off bridges, slit his wrists, overdosed on pills, and even tried to hang himself. But each time, something intervened. A gust of wind would blow him off the bridge before he could jump. His wrists would heal before he could bleed out. The pills would make him vomit before they could kill him. The rope would break before he could suffocate. It was like the universe was telling him that it wasn't his time yet. That he had something left to do. But the man couldn't figure out what that was. He was tired of living, tired of trying to kill himself. He just wanted to die. But the universe seemed to have other plans.

If you're considering a career in software engineering, there's a lot you need to know that they don't teach you in school. For starters, you need to be proficient in multiple coding languages, as well as be able to understand complicated algorithms. You must also be able to work with teams of other engineers to develop large-scale projects. But it's not all code all the time. As a software engineer, you'll also need to have excellent communication skills. You'll be working with clients, project managers, and other engineers to ensure that everyone is on the same page and that the project is moving forward as planned. There's a lot of pressure that comes with the job, as well. Deadlines are often tight, and you'll need to be able to work quickly and efficiently under pressure. But despite all of the challenges, being a software engineer can be an incredibly rewarding career. You'll get to work on cutting-edge technologies, solve complex problems, and see your projects come to life. If you're up for the challenge, a career in software engineering might just be for you.

I was walking home from work one day, minding my own business, when suddenly the sky began to rumble and a powerful voice boomed out across the city. "You have been chosen," it declared. I stopped in my tracks, unsure of what to think. I had no idea what was going on or who was speaking. Then, the voice continued. "You are the new narrator of a popular series," it said. I was baffled. I'd never even heard of this series before. How could I possibly be chosen to narrate it? The voice spoke again. "The gods of the series have chosen you to take the place of the former narrator, who recently passed away," it explained. "Your task is to continue the story and keep it alive." I was filled with both excitement and trepidation. It was an amazing opportunity, but I knew nothing about this series. How was I supposed to do this? I walked into the world of the series, slowly getting to know the characters and the story. As I did, I began to alter little things here and there- adding my own spin to the narrative. At first, the characters were confused by my changes, but gradually they began to appreciate them. They realized that these alterations were helping them to become more rounded and developed individuals. Soon enough, the series became a sensation and I was praised for my creativity and skill. I was filled with joy and satisfaction, knowing that I had managed to take something that I had never even heard of and make it my own.

Frequent pattern mining is a key area of study that gives insights into the structure and dynamics of evolving networks, such as social or road networks. However, not only does real-world data tend to be noisy, but it is also often incomplete. For example, in social networks, users might be reluctant to reveal the complete set of their friends, so that the network to be mined contains only partial information. A lot of work has been devoted to the problem of mining patterns from such incomplete data. Although a number of methods have been proposed, they are all quite limited in their ability to mine the most important classes of patterns (e.g., maximal cliques) in large, real-world networks. In this paper, we present a new algorithm for mining maximal cliques from incomplete networks. Our approach is based on formulating the problem as an integer linear program, and then solving it using standard optimization techniques. We evaluate our algorithm on both synthetic and real-world data, and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin. end{abstract} section{Introduction} Frequent pattern mining is a key area of study that gives insights into the structure and dynamics of evolving networks, such as social or road networks. Mr Maduro said the room would be kept intact and a wing of the presidential palace turned into a monument to Mr Chavez's "Bolivarian revolution." Mr Chavez died of cancer on March 5. "This room is going to remain as a monument to the life of President Chavez," Mr Maduro said. "It's going to be an emotional and spiritual shrine." Mr Chavez had been in hospital for more than two months before his death, and his absence from public view sparked rumours about his health. He was diagnosed with an undisclosed form of cancer in mid-2011 and had a tumour removed from his pelvic area. The following year he underwent two more operations, chemotherapy and radiation treatments. In December 2012, following a fourth round of surgery in Cuba, Mr Chavez announced that doctors had found no evidence of cancer in his body and that he had been "totally cured." But in April last year, he confirmed that the illness had returned and that he would need another operation. The surgery was successful but he never fully recovered and died in a military hospital in Caracas at 58. Mr Maduro has vowed to continue Mr Chavez's socialist policies and is leading a snap presidential election on April 14. He is expected to win comfortably against opposition leader Henrique Capriles.

Joe thought it was ridiculous to waste time sitting by the lake. He'd rather be doing something fun! But his mother insisted the family watch the sunset together. He was reluctant at first, but eventually decided to give it a chance. As they sat by the calm waters, admiring the beautiful colors of the sun setting, Joe began to relax and appreciate the peacefulness of the moment. He even started to notice little things he hadn't before, like a family of ducks swimming by or the way the water reflected the orange and pink hues of the sky. By the end of the sunset, Joe realized that taking a break and enjoying the stillness of nature can be just as fun and exciting as any other activity.

A leading human rights organisation has urged Nato to investigate fully the deaths of civilians in air strikes in Libya last year. The organisation, Human Rights Watch, says it has uncovered evidence that at least two civilians were killed in separate incidents during the conflict. It has called on Nato to carry out a full and transparent investigation into the deaths, and to make the findings public. The call comes as Nato prepares to mark the end of its mission in Libya, which began last March. Human Rights Watch says the two civilians who were killed were both women. One was killed in an air strike on a house in the town of Brega, while the other died in an attack on a convoy near the town of Sirte. In both cases, the organisation says, there is evidence that the targets of the attacks were military, but that civilians were killed as a result. Nato has said it will not comment on the specific allegations until it has seen the full report from Human Rights Watch. However, a spokesman said the alliance takes all allegations of civilian casualties "very seriously."

Tommy was a little boy who hated soup. He thought it was gross and slimy and he didn't like the way it smelled. Whenever his mom would make soup, he would hold his nose and try not to gag. Tommy's friends would always make fun of him and call him a baby because he didn't like soup. One day, Tommy's mom made him a bowl of soup and he accidentally dropped it on the floor. Tommy started to cry and his mom got mad. She told him that he was never allowed to have soup again. Tommy was so happy that he danced around the house. From then on, Tommy was known as the "weird soup thing" but he didn't care. He was just glad he would never have to eat soup again.

In 2000, ABC launched a web-based promotional campaign focused around its circle logo, also called "the dot," in which comic book character Little Dot prompted visitors to "download the dot," referring to the QuickTime plug-in. "The dot" (referring to the ABC logo), is a term commonly used by the network's sports commentators. During the early 1990s, the network ran a series of promotions that asked viewers to identify the slogan "There's Always Something Good on ABC," with a chance to win a prize. The slogan was retired in 2000, as part of the network's move away from its family-friendly image and toward edgier programming. In May 2006, ABC launched its first ever on-air promotion for the network's website ABC.com. The 60-second spot, entitled "Download," begins with a girl waking up and going downstairs. Upon sitting down at her computer, she clicks on "ABC.com" in her browser, which opens the ABC home page. A problem is regarded as inherently difficult if its solution requires significant resources, whatever the algorithm used. The theory formalizes this intuition, by introducing mathematical models of computation to study these problems and quantifying the amount of resources needed to solve them, such as time and storage. Problems that are considered inherently difficult include NP-Complete problems, which cannot be solved in polynomial time (i.e., using an algorithm that takes a certain number of steps that grows linearly with the size of the problem). This means that, even if a more efficient algorithm were discovered, it would still require exponential time to solve the problem. Other examples of inherently difficult problems include the traveling salesman problem, the graph isomorphism problem, and the Boolean satisfiability problem.

The Earth is constantly changing and moving in predictable patterns and cycles. The water cycle and nutrient cycles (carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur, etc.) are Earth's metabolism. The Homo sapiens component of Earth's metabolism is the human economy. The water cycle is one of the most important metabolic processes on Earth. It is the process by which water circulates through the atmosphere, lithosphere, and hydrosphere. The water cycle is driven by the sun, which evaporates water from the surface of the earth. This water vapor condenses into clouds, which precipitate onto the surface of the earth, where it eventually returns to the oceans. The water cycle is essential for life on Earth. It provides the water that we drink, bathe in, and irrigate our crops with. It also helps to regulate the Earth's temperature by transferring heat from the equator to the poles. The carbon cycle is another important metabolic process on Earth. It is the process by which carbon is circulated through the atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere. The carbon cycle is driven by the sun, which photosynthesizes plants, which convert carbon dioxide into oxygen. This oxygen is used by animals to breathe, and the carbon dioxide is exhaled back into the atmosphere. The carbon cycle is essential for life on Earth. It provides the carbon that we use to make food, fuel, and other products. It also helps to regulate the Earth's climate by absorbing greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide. The nitrogen cycle is the process by which nitrogen is circulated through the atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere. The nitrogen cycle is driven by bacteria, which convert nitrogen gas into nitrates, which are used by plants to grow. Animals eat plants, and the nitrogen is returned to the atmosphere when they breathe out. The nitrogen cycle is essential for life on Earth. It provides the nitrogen that we need to make food, fuel, and other products. It also helps to regulate the Earth's climate by reducing greenhouse gases such as nitrogen oxide. The sulfur cycle is the process by which sulfur is circulated through the atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere. The sulfur cycle is driven by volcanoes, which emit sulfur dioxide gas into the atmosphere. This gas is converted into sulfates by bacteria, which are then rain down onto the surface of the Earth. Plants and animals use sulfates to grow, and the sulfur is returned to the atmosphere when they breathe out. The sulfur cycle is essential for life on Earth. It provides the sulfur that we need to make food, fuel, and other products. It also helps to regulate the Earth's climate by reducing greenhouse gases such as sulfur dioxide.

A charity has warned that thousands of elderly people in the UK are missing out on free personal care due to delays to assessments and care arrangements. Age UK say that vital services, such as getting help with washing and dressing, have been put at risk because of delays to assessments which determine whether or not a person is eligible for free care. The charity also highlighted that, in some cases, there have been significant delays in arranging and implementing care plans. Caroline Abrahams, Age UK's Charity Director, said: "It's unacceptable that vulnerable older people are having to wait so long to get the support they need. This is causing distress and anxiety and exacerbating the loneliness and isolation many face." The charity is calling on local authorities to speed up the assessment process and ensure that the most vulnerable elderly people get the care and support they are entitled to. They are also urging the government to increase funding for social care and provide additional resources for councils to ensure the process is efficient and timely. Age UK's research found that one in four councils had experienced delays of over six months in assessments and care arrangements, while one in 10 councils reported delays of more than nine months. Furthermore, the charity estimates that, based on the data collected, around 100,000 elderly people may be missing out on free care due to these delays. Ms Abrahams added: "We know how hard it is for many local authorities to meet their legal obligations to assess and arrange care for older people but that doesn't change the fact that this situation is causing real hardship for older people who are unable to get the care they need."

The startup has raised 67 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Spark Capital, and Bezos Expeditions, the venture capital firm of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. With the acquisition, Snap is betting that BCI will eventually become a key input method for its AR glasses. The company has been working on a pair of AR glasses, codenamed "Project Spectacles," for several years, and is expected to launch a beta version of the product later this year. So far, BCI technology has been used primarily for research purposes. But a number of startups are working on commercial applications, including Ctrl-labs. The startup's wristband, which is still in development, uses electromyography (EMG) to detect electrical activity in the wearer's arm muscles. This information is then translated into digital commands that can be used to control AR experiences, or even real-world objects like drones and robots. The wristband is not yet available to consumers, butCtrl-labs has been working with a number of partners, including Facebook, on potential applications for the technology. With the acquisition, Snap will gain access to Ctrl-labs' technology and team of engineers and scientists. As there had been only six British monarchs during that time, these are the names by which the conflict is most commonly known. The French colonists named their war in North America La guerre de la Conquete the War of Conquest. It also became known as the Fourth Indian War or in New England as the Fourth Intercolonial War. The Great Peace of Montreal of 1701 was signed on August 4, 1701, by Louis-Hector de Calliere, governor general of New France, and representatives of 39 Indigenous nations. It ended a century of armed conflicts between the French and Iroquois Confederacy, preventing the expansion of the Iroquois Confederacy south and west into Iroquoian territory and halting almost all Iroquois raids into French territory and their allies for the next 50 years. It was also an attempt to create a formal peace among the Iroquois and several other First Nations that engaged in the Beaver Wars. In the aftermath of the Three Fires Confederation's victory in the Beaver Wars, they gained control over the trade routes of the Great Lakes. With this increased power, they were able to extract higher prices from the French to obtain goods. They also attempted to expand their territory at the expense of neighboring tribes. King William's War (1688-97), also known as the Second Indian War, Father Baudoin's War, or Castin's War, was the North American theater of the Nine Years' War (1688-97). It was the first of six colonial wars fought between New France and New England along with their respective Native allies before France ceded its remaining mainland territories in North America east of the Mississippi River in 1763 under the terms of the Treaty of Paris. For King William's War, neither England nor France thought of weakening their position in Europe to support the war effort in North America. New France and the Wabanaki Confederacy were able to thwart New England expansion into Acadia, whose border New France defined as the Kennebec River in southern Maine. The outbreak of King William's War had largely been precipitated by the efforts of Massachusetts, Plymouth, and Maine to coerce the Wabanaki Confederacy into ceding Acadia. Through much of the war, the Wabanaki Confederacy continued to supply Acadia with food and furs in exchange for French guns and ammunition. The primary opposition to this expansion came from the Mi'kmaq and Abenaki, who were members of the Wabanaki Confederacy. They were joined by Acadians, French settlers, and a small number of Dutch colonies. Despite early Massachusetts victories in King William's War, the Wabanaki Confederacy and other allies returned the favor in the following Queen Anne's War. They took back Acadia, expelling British settlers along with New England troops. Following the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht, Acadia was officially returned to France, but the treaty left the border undefined. A crown colony was then established along the Kennebec River in late 1722, called Nova Scotia. Its capital was intended to be located at Port Royal, which had been serving as the capital of Acadia since 1605. However, given the hostility of the Wabanaki Confederacy toward the establishment of a British colony along the Kennebec River, Governor Richard Philipps preferred to establish his capital elsewhere. King William's War began on June 24, 1689 when King William III issued a royal proclamation declaring war against France and putting into effect the Anglo-French War Declaration of 1688. It ended with the Treaty of Ryswick in 1697. Along with the other conflicts that arose in Europe, this conflict played a significant role in the development of the colonies of North America. King William's War resulted in the French losing Acadia and gave the British a foothold in Newfoundland and Maine. It was the second of four North American wars that formed the European phase of the Nine Years' War. The Lachine massacre was a battle that took place on 5 August 1689, during King William's War, at present-day Lachine, Quebec, Canada. On that day, 800 Iroquois warriors attacked a 200-strong garrison of French soldiers and 100 Huron and Algonquin militiamen, killing or wounding approximately 150 of them. The rest of the garrison was taken prisoner, including Governor Jacques de Callieres, who had arrived from Montreal just days before. The Iroquois then plundered the nearby town of Lachine and set fire to all its buildings, before returning to their village at La Montagne. The Lachine massacre shocked New France, paralyzing settlement and leading to a near-total abandonment of the western portion of the colony. This allows the system to dynamically adapt its architecture to changes in environment, workloads or operating conditions without having to replace the underlying hardware. In addition, it also enables the system to perform runtime optimizations and to take advantage of new technologies without having to modify the existing hardware. The use of adaptive systems has been gaining popularity in recent years, particularly in the field of embedded systems where its flexibility is beneficial for applications that require dynamic adaptation. A human rights organisation has urged Nato to investigate the deaths of civilians in air strikes in Libya last year. The organisation, which has not been named, said that an initial inquiry by Nato had been "inadequate." It is thought that at least 70 civilians were killed in Nato air strikes during the conflict in Libya. Nato has said that it takes great care to avoid civilian casualties and that its strikes are directed only at military targets. However, the human rights organisation said that some of the attacks appeared to be "disproportionate" and called for a full and independent investigation. The organisation's report is based on interviews with more than 100 witnesses and survivors of the air strikes, as well as analysis of video footage and satellite images. The BBC has seen a copy of the report, which is due to be published later this week.

The leading human rights organisation, Human Rights Watch (HRW), has called on Nato to launch a full investigation into the deaths of civilians in air strikes in Libya last year. The call comes after HRW reported that at least 72 civilians were killed in 14 separate airstrikes during Nato's campaign against Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi in 2011. The strikes were part of Nato's mission, authorised by the United Nations Security Council, to protect Libyan civilians from Gaddafi's forces. In a statement released yesterday, HRW said that it had conducted "extensive field investigations" into the airstrikes and had identified "serious questions about the accuracy of Nato's targeting of military targets in populated areas." It added that further investigation was needed to determine whether or not civilian casualties could have been avoided. Nato's Secretary General Anders Fogh Rasmussen responded to the HRW statement, saying that "every effort was made to avoid civilian casualties" during the campaign. He added that the Alliance had conducted its own investigations into reports of civilian casualties and had determined that these were "unavoidable due to the extreme circumstances." However, HRW's executive director Kenneth Roth insisted that Nato should conduct a "proper, independent investigation with full public disclosure" of its findings. He added that the international community had a responsibility to ensure that all parties involved in armed conflicts comply with international law. This latest call for an investigation adds to the growing pressure on Nato to look into the events of last year's conflict in Libya. Civilian casualties are an emotive subject and with the new government in place, the Libyan people are likely to demand answers over the deaths of innocent bystanders.

With the increasing penetration of renewable energy resources, power systems face new challenges in maintaining power balance and the nominal frequency. This paper studies load control to handle these challenges. We model the problem of optimal real power dispatch in a power system with renewable resources as a nonlinear optimization problem. The objective is to minimize the total cost, which includes the cost of generation and load control. We consider three different types of loads: controllable loads, uncontrollable loads, and loads with price elasticity. We show that the optimal solution of our problem can be found by solving a convex optimization problem. Numerical experiments are conducted on a modified IEEE 14 bus system to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method. Results show that the proposed load control approach can effectively reduce the total cost of generation and load control. Our proposed method also offers a better solution compared to the traditional methods such as economic dispatch and direct load control. Furthermore, our proposed method is suitable for dealing with the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources in modern power systems.

To do so: Click on the profile logo or icon located at the top right corner of your screen. Select "Policy Info" from the drop down menu. [visible-phone] [collapse] [title] Please Note Your insurer will likely require that you provide documentation to back up your need to add an interested party. [title] Related: How to add an additional interest to your insurance policy How to cancel homeowners insurance What's the difference between an additional interest and an interested party? Additional interests and interested parties are both entities that have a financial interest in the property protected by your policy. Your homeowner's insurance policy is designed to protect your financial interest in the property, whichever entity that may be. However, an additional interest is not legally entitled to notice of cancellation or nonrenewal of the policy, or any other documents related to the policy. An interested party is legally entitled to notice of cancellation or nonrenewal of the policy, as well as any other documents related to the policy, such as renewals and endorsements. An additional interest can be added to your policy either at inception or after the fact. On the other hand, an interested party can only be added to your policy after it's been issued.

We consider the problem of learning a non-deterministic probabilistic system consistent with a given finite set of positive and negative tree samples. Consistency is defined with respect to strong simulation equivalence and we assume that the system is represented as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). We propose an approach based on Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) which uses a set of tree samples to generate a set of sample transitions, denoted by mathcal{T}, which are then used to estimate the MDP parameters. Specifically, we use the Expectation Maximization algorithm to iteratively refine the estimates of the parameters. This approach requires no prior knowledge of the system and thus can be used in any setting. We evaluate our approach on two case studies taken from robotics: one involving a robot navigating in an environment with obstacles and another involving a robot performing complex manipulation tasks. We show that our approach is able to recover the parameters of the MDP accurately. Our results demonstrate that MLE can be used for learning non-deterministic probabilistic systems from data.

The notion "force" keeps its meaning in quantum mechanics, though one is now dealing with operators instead of classical variables and though the physics is now described by the Schrodinger equation. In quantum mechanics, force is still a physical quantity that affects the motion of particles. However, the mathematical description of this force is different than in classical mechanics. In quantum mechanics, forces are described by the interaction of particles with fields, which are represented by quantum mechanical operators. These operators act on the wave functions of the particles to describe how they are affected by the force. So while the concept of force remains relevant in quantum mechanics, its description and the mathematics used to describe it are different from classical mechanics.

The smaller one fell to the ground and didn't move. I watched in horror as the tall one stepped back, surveying the scene with a satisfied smirk on his face. Then he turned and walked away, leaving me alone with the lifeless body. In that moment, I realized that I had witnessed a murder. My cheerful disposition had been replaced with shock and fear. Terra preta (black earth), which is distributed over large areas in the Amazon forest, is now widely accepted as a product of indigenous soil management. The development of this fertile earth layer is associated with the formation of charcoal residues in the soil. This has thus far only been possible by extensive laboratory methods, which are largely unsuitable for routine use. The aim of our study was to develop a rapid method for the detection of charcoal in soils with a view to identifying terra preta. Several samples were taken from cultivated and uncultivated soils in the vicinity of two indigenous tribes in the Amazon region, which were then analysed using X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy (XRF). In addition, backscattered electron images (BSEI) were recorded and the results were verified by means of transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Compared with TEM and XRF measurements, this method proved to be suitable for detecting charcoal residues in the soil. Thus, areas that are potentially suitable for terra preta can be quickly and easily identified using this method. The current gold standard for human activity recognition (HAR) is based on the use of cameras. However, the poor scalability of camera systems renders them impractical in pursuit of the real-time recognition of human activities in everyday environments. Therefore, there is a need for alternative methods that can be used for HAR in everyday environments where vision-based systems are impractical because of their limited scalability. In this paper we propose the use of WiFi signals for this purpose. WiFi signals are ubiquitous and have already been successfully employed for indoor localization. We exploit the WiFi signal strength measurements to construct a feature space that captures both spatial and temporal information. We then use a Support Vector Machine (SVM) to classify the activities. Our method is tested on two publicly available datasets: the WISDM dataset and the MobiAct dataset. The results show that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods for activity recognition using WiFi signals.

Stanford University researchers have discovered a breakthrough method to create diamonds at a much faster and easier rate than ever before. The process, which involves "cheating the thermodynamics," was published in the journal Nature Communications. Traditional diamond-making techniques require immense pressure and heat under the Earth's surface, but the Stanford researchers have found a way to create diamonds in just minutes using a process called plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition. By combining methane gas and hydrogen gas with a microwave plasma, the team was able to create a diamond film on a silicon wafer. The result is a high-quality diamond, which can be used for industrial purposes. According to Peter Pauzauskie, an assistant professor of materials science and engineering at Stanford, the breakthrough method could significantly reduce the cost of diamond production and lower the environmental impact of diamond mining. "This method of diamond creation is more energy-efficient and less damaging to the environment, as it doesn't require the significant resources and labor associated with traditional diamond mining," Pauzauskie said. The researchers hope that the findings will pave the way for more sustainable and accessible diamond production in the future. Already, the technology has attracted interest from both the industrial and jewelry sectors. "This is a game-changer for the diamond industry," said Pauzauskie. "Our method allows for the creation of high-quality diamonds at a much faster and easier rate, which could revolutionize the way we produce and consume diamonds." While the team acknowledges that the method is not yet able to produce large gem-quality diamonds, they believe that this breakthrough could lead to advancements in diamond technology and applications across a range of industries.

Knowledge graphs capture entities and relations from long documents and can facilitate reasoning in many downstream applications. Extracting compact knowledge graphs containing only salient entities and relations is important but can be challenging. There are many techniques and approaches that can be used to extract knowledge graphs, including natural language processing, machine learning, and graph mining techniques. Natural language processing techniques can be used to extract entities and relations from textual data, such as named entity recognition, entity disambiguation, and relation extraction. These techniques rely on language models and ontologies to understand the meaning of the text and identify entities and their relationships. Machine learning techniques can also be used to extract knowledge graphs, including supervised and unsupervised learning methods. Supervised learning techniques rely on labeled datasets to train models to identify entities and relations, while unsupervised learning techniques can learn patterns and relationships in data without prior labeling. Graph mining techniques can be applied to extract structural patterns from data and identify entities and relations based on their connectivity in a graph. These techniques can be combined with machine learning and natural language processing techniques for more accurate and comprehensive knowledge graph extraction. Overall, selecting the appropriate techniques and approaches for knowledge graph extraction will depend on the specific use case and data available.

It is believed the attacker drove over Westminster Bridge in his car at around 14:40 GMT and hit several pedestrians. He then crashed into the perimeter fence of Parliament and ran through the gates, armed with two knives. At around 15:00 GMT he stabbed PC Keith Palmer before being shot dead by armed police. Authorities say four people died in total, including the attacker and PC Palmer. More than 40 others were injured. What do we know about the attacker? The Metropolitan Police said the attacker was British-born but would not name him. One government source told the BBC that police had identified the man and informed his family, but did not wish to release his name. Speaking in the Commons, Prime Minister Theresa May said: "The man was British-born and some years ago was once investigated by MI5 in relation to concerns about violent extremism." She said he had been a "peripheral" figure and there was "no prior intelligence of his intent to attack." The BBC understands that the attacker was not a current target for either MI5 or police counter-terrorism officers. So far the police have given few details about the attacker's identity. This appears to differ from the Manchester Arena bombing last Monday, when Salman Abedi was named within hours of the attack. The authorities say there are differences in cases like these. A lone attacker can be much more difficult to investigate and prevent than a terror cell. The fact that this attacker was born here also complicates matters. How will the investigation unfold? In investigations like this, every piece of information is vital. While the Westminster attacker's movements and methods are now understood, the police will need to uncover his motivation. This means looking at any contacts he had, whether it was with friends and family or with other extremists. The police will also want to find out if he was radicalised online or elsewhere. He is thought to have worked as a teacher, although the schools he taught in have not been named. Police raids have taken place near Birmingham primary schools and one secondary school. Wherever he lived, he will have left a trail. Several websites have been blocked, accused of celebrating the attack. In the past, social media has been crucial in providing information about terror suspects. Detectives will also want to look at anything the attacker wrote down - whether it was a notebook, diary or even a shopping list. At any given time, the security services and police are investigating about 3,000 people suspected of terrorism. Most of these are linked to Islamist extremism and are being watched closely. This paper provides the extension of the observability rank condition and the extension of the controllability rank condition to time-varying nonlinear systems. Previous conditions to check the state observability and controllability of nonlinear systems were only applicable to time-invariant systems, but this paper presents a new method to extend these conditions to time-varying systems. The observability rank condition is used to determine whether the states of a system can be fully inferred from the available measurements. The controllability rank condition is used to determine whether it is possible to steer the system from any initial state to any desired state using the available inputs. In this paper, the authors use Lie derivatives and Lie brackets to derive the extended observability and controllability rank conditions for time-varying nonlinear systems. These conditions provide a way to check the state observability and controllability of time-varying nonlinear systems. The authors present a few examples to demonstrate the applicability of the extended rank conditions for nonlinear systems. The results obtained from the examples show that the extended rank conditions are useful in designing control strategies for time-varying nonlinear systems. In summary, the paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of control systems by extending the observability and controllability rank conditions to time-varying nonlinear systems. This will enable researchers and practitioners to have a better understanding of the observability and controllability properties of such systems, leading to the development of more effective control strategies.

He also sought to eliminate the veneration of saints, which he felt distracted from the central figure of Jesus Christ. He encouraged the use of the German language in worship and promoted the singing of hymns in the vernacular. Finally, he called for the reform of clerical life, insisting that priests lead exemplary lives and focus on their pastoral duties. In 1530 Luther drew up his Ninety-Five Theses, a document that contained his criticisms of the Catholic Church and its practices. This was the first public statement of Luther's beliefs and it sparked a religious revolution that would see the Protestant Reformation sweep across Europe. Luther's reforms spread quickly and within a few decades had become firmly entrenched in many parts of Europe. These changes brought about by Luther's reforms had a profound effect on not just religious life but also on politics, culture and society.

The ePlane is powered by a magni500 propulsion system developed by magniX, an aerospace technology company based in Redmond, Washington. The company has been working for years to develop electric aircraft propulsion systems and said that the successful flight marks a "significant step forward" in its mission to create affordable, zero-emission air travel. The flight took off from the Fraser River near Vancouver, British Columbia and demonstrated the plane's ability to take off, fly, and land safely. It is the first of many test flights planned as part of the certification process for the electric aircraft. McDougall said that the successful flight was an important step in a long journey towards sustainable aviation. He noted that the transition to electric aircraft will require significant infrastructure investments, but that the payoff would be worth it. "We believe that the transition to electric aircraft will make air travel more accessible, reduce the environmental impact, and ultimately make air travel safer," he said. Harbour Air and magniX said they plan to continue testing the aircraft and hope to have it certified for commercial use by 2021. If successful, the ePlane could revolutionize air travel, reducing emissions and opening up new possibilities for low-cost and sustainable air transportation.
